summary: Long observation by car of 8 to 10 white luminous phenomena photographs: observation of reflections of the sun through the windshield.
description: On December 29, 2012, at 1:05 PM, two people in a car were intrigued by the presence of 8 to 10 white luminous phenomena seen through the windshield in the clear sky. No noise was heard during the entire observation. Only one witness statement was collected, and the witness sent GEIPAN a set of photographs taken with their cell phone. The photos show various shapes of varying brightness: the witness does not specify which of these artifacts they saw with the naked eye. Indeed, the annotated photo shows various reflections on the camera lens or on the windshield; with the naked eye, the witness could see the reflections on the windshield, but they likely discovered even more surprising effects in the photos. Given the observation conditions—in a car facing south, at the zenith, close to the winter solstice—the conditions are ideal for observing multiple reflections of the sun on windows or lenses. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of sun reflections through the windshield.

summary: Observation of several luminous phenomena at very low altitude including 8 flashing rectangular spots: probable observation of headlight reflections on the car windows.
description: On December 28, 2012, at 9:45 PM, a witness driving on the A61 motorway near the Toulouse-Sud rest area observed a very close, stationary luminous phenomenon for 20 to 30 seconds, which intrigued him. He saw two horizontal white lights at a very low altitude, then a central white beam illuminating the ground. These lights went out and were replaced by 6 to 8 rectangular spotlights that flashed successively in yellow and orange. The witness stopped at a service station, but trees obscured his view of the phenomenon. Despite the heavy traffic on the motorway that evening, no other witness statements were collected. The difficulty in this case lies in the single witness statement in an otherwise very busy area, which makes it difficult to fully understand the phenomenon. The search for other witnesses proved unsuccessful, even though the phenomenon was quite spectacular (see the investigation report). The observation was very brief and took place in a car traveling at night on a heavily congested highway. The witness is sincere and was so impressed by what he saw that he returned to the scene the next day, went to the Muret gendarmerie, and sent a letter to GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Information and Prevention Group). His testimony is relatively precise but unique. The hypothesis of reflections combined with poor perception or interpretation seems the most likely but does not call into question the witness's credibility. This case is classified as Class B: probable observation of headlight reflections on the car windows.

summary: Observation of the silent rectilinear and upward movement of luminous phenomena of red-orange colour; instantaneous extinction of some: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 24, 2012, at approximately 9:45 PM, a family observed six to eight luminous points of light, ranging in color from red to orange-yellow, moving silently for five minutes. They appeared successively at the same frequency and seemed to follow each other at equal distances in the sky. All followed an upward trajectory. Some disappeared instantly. A witness recorded a video. The witnesses' observations were characteristic of a Thai lantern release, both in terms of colors, shapes, trajectory, and the fact that the lanterns extinguished mid-flight. The rapid south-to-north movement corresponds to the wind measured in Biarritz (record of a fairly strong southerly wind on infoclimat). The first two UFOs differ in their direction of movement (east to west), but these directions are reported to the witness and are not the witness's own; they do not benefit from the extra attention or precision involved in completing a questionnaire or witness statement, and furthermore, near the ocean, the wind can be unstable. Finally, the date and time, the evening of December 24th, support the hypothesis of Thai lanterns, as this is conducive to a festive balloon-licking event. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: lanterns Thai women.

summary: Observation for three seconds of a luminous phenomenon illuminating the sky: probable atmospheric reentry of a bolide.
description: On December 17, 2012, at 11:30 PM, a witness from their home suddenly saw the sky light up with a deep blue for three seconds. This account is very brief; the witness only saw a powerful flash indirectly. The color and duration of the phenomenon are consistent with a bolide (atmospheric re-entry of a meteoroid), probably linked to the Geminid meteor shower, which was particularly noteworthy that year (see http://clubregulus.free.fr/geminides.html). One could also consider an electrical lightning strike (electrical welding equipment, a major short circuit on a power line); however, the witness did not report the usual flashing of electrical lightning but rather a complete illumination of the sky (which was overcast), which is consistent with a high-altitude phenomenon. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of a bolide.

summary: Observation of the movement of a dark triangular craft above a dwelling; buzzing and clicking noise and rapid disappearance: lack of information.
description: This is an older case (2012), reported in August 2014. An investigator contacted the witness by telephone and then met with them in December 2014, allowing the witness to supplement their statement. On December 14, 2012, around 5:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by a shadow that obscured the living room window. Going out onto their terrace, the person observed a black object moving above their home. The witness described a triangular object with overlapping side panels and a circular shape in its center. Steam was escaping from the object. During the 2- to 4-minute observation, buzzing and "clacking" noises were heard. The witness signaled towards the object, and it immediately disappeared rapidly to the northwest. No other statements were collected. After investigation, this very strange sighting, reminiscent of an unknown craft, but reported by only one witness and 20 months after the event, proves insufficiently substantial to provide a solid scientific opinion (see the investigation report). The case is classified as category C due to a lack of sufficient information related to its strangeness.

summary: Observation by a pilot of the East-West passage of a green phenomenon: probable meteoroid fall.
description: pilot reported an observation made in flight: on December 13, 2012, at 4:48 PM UTC, he observed (in the Toulouse 030 runway) the east-west passage of a green meteorite at an estimated altitude between 45,000 and 60,000 ft. The brief description suggests a meteoroid re-entry into the atmosphere (meteorite fall). This time of year corresponds to the peak of the Geminid meteor shower (coming from the northeast horizon at this time). Numerous observations were made on December 12 and 13 by automatic cameras and observers. However, GEIPAN received no other simultaneous reports. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of a meteoroid fall.

summary: Observations of a yellow-orange luminous phenomenon in the sky: flare used during military training.
description: On December 12, 2012, at 7:20 PM (UTC), a pilot and a controller were intrigued by the presence of a bright yellow-orange light in the sky. A photograph was taken from the aircraft. The phenomenon was also seen by a ground observer at Espira de l'Agly (66) the same day. Local inquiries at the nearby military base revealed that training exercises had taken place there two evenings in a row using flares. This clearly defined case is therefore classified as "A".

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous ball in the sky preceded by a muffled noise: probable observation of a bolide.
description: Around 7:00 AM on December 12, 2012, a witness was intrigued by a muffled sound and then observed a luminous phenomenon followed by the rapid passage of a blue or yellow fireball. No trail was seen. The account of the observation clearly evokes the appearance of a large fireball: a powerful luminous phenomenon lasting a few seconds, accompanied by a sound. The date of the event is very close to the peak of the Geminid meteor shower. The BOAM (http://www.boam.fr) reports the recording of numerous events of this type at that time (the cameras are installed in northern France and probably did not capture this fireball, which was located south of Toulouse). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of a fireball, probably from the Geminid meteor shower.

summary: Observation of the movement of a powerful colored luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of a bolide.
description: On December 12, 2012, at 8:10 PM, a witness observed a silent, 10-second flash of light across the sky. The account of the observation clearly describes the appearance of a large fireball: a powerful, blue, luminous phenomenon lasting a few seconds, caused by the entry into the atmosphere of a meteoroid (asteroid) or satellite debris. The date of the event is very close to the peak of the Geminid meteor shower. The BOAM (http://www.boam.fr) reports the recording of numerous events of this type during this period, but not at this exact time. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of a fireball, probably originating from the Geminid meteor shower.

summary: Observation of a stationary and silent luminous phenomenon in the sky: lack of information.
description: On December 5, 2012, at approximately 9:45 PM, a witness from their sixth-floor apartment observed a very bright object in the clear sky, concealing a dark-colored craft. This object remained stationary for about ten minutes without any sound before disappearing. No other witness accounts of this phenomenon were collected. This observation is quite strange, and it is also very surprising that it was reported by only one person, despite the city's high population density. Following the gendarmerie's investigation, which carefully verified information with aviation and security authorities, GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group) wished to conduct an on-site investigation with the witness, but he declined. Due to the impossibility of conducting this investigation, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" for lack of information.

summary: Observation of the movement of red lights in the sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: In the early hours of Sunday, December 2nd, at 12:03 AM, a couple observed from their home about ten bright red objects following one another at regular intervals and disappearing one after the other into the cloudy sky. The witness's description corresponds to the appearance of Thai lanterns (although the description also noted bluish reflections, rare on lanterns, unless they were blue). The local wind, as recorded in Verneuil, was light and unstable (see readings) from the west, consistent with the movement of these objects. They may have been released along the banks of the Seine at the end of a festive evening. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation in the Parisian sky of the hovering flight then the slow rectilinear movement of a grey triangular object with flashing red lights: probable observation of a giant fantasy balloon equipped with LEDs.
description: On December 1, 2012, at 5:00 PM, a witness observed a stationary gray object in the Parisian sky. The witness described the object as triangular but also as a spinning top with "a pointed tip at the nose and a cross shape in the center." No noise or smoke was observed. The object then moved slowly, as if carried by the wind, always at the same altitude. The witness then saw several flashing red lights aligned in the center of the craft. During the observation, the witness took a photograph. No other witness statements were collected. Given the objective elements gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - Object moving with the wind. - Shape and color consistent with existing models of novelty balloons. - Size and distance estimates consistent with each other. We can conclude that the UFO observed and photographed by the witness could be a novelty balloon model in the shape of a fighter jet, moving with the wind. This case is to be classified as B as a probable observation of a novelty balloon equipped with LEDs.

summary: Testimony in 2014 of an observation made in 2012 of the rapid evolutions of an intense white and red luminous phenomenon at low altitude: lack of information.
description: 2014 report of a previous sighting. On November 29, 2012, at 6:40 PM, a witness observed, in the distance, towards the East-Southeast, the unusual and rapid movements (ascending, descending, with changes of direction, with division) of an intense, red and white light at low altitude in the cloudy sky. No other reports were collected. This report is based on little information; the questionnaire was only partially completed (e.g., duration and speed not indicated, only one UFO position given despite mentioning movement), and the photos mentioned were never provided despite follow-up requests from GEIPAN. The report concerns a sighting from two years prior. As it stands, it is not possible to respond to this report. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.

summary: Long observations of a luminous phenomenon above the sea: observation of the lighting of a boat.
description: On November 25, 2012, two witnesses observed a point of light between the Gaou peninsula and the Embiez islands from the clifftop of Fort de la Collegiale. Intrigued, they observed this phenomenon for approximately three hours. During the investigation, the invaluable assistance of an employee from the Marine Traffic department proved crucial. He enabled the clear identification of the "Mol Marvel," a container ship sailing south of Toulon. This was indeed the ship seen by the witnesses at the date and time corresponding to its passage in the indicated direction. Its size, speed, and distance from the coastline are entirely consistent with the witness statements and photographs taken (see the "investigation notes" document). GEIPAN classifies this case as Category A (perfectly identified phenomenon): observation of a ship's lights.

summary: Observations of a bright, fixed light in the sky; then moving: very probable observations of an aircraft seen head-on, approaching Le Havre-Octeville.
description: On November 22, 2012, at approximately 9:15 PM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a bright, steady light in the overcast sky. Then, around 9:24 PM, he noticed the light moving slowly and horizontally in the direction of Fontenay. The witness's mother also saw the steady light, "like a spotlight," but saw no flashing lights. The light disappeared, hidden by the rooftops of houses. No other witness statements were collected. The gendarmerie conducted a thorough investigation with military air traffic control, neighboring police stations, the Octeville airport, and Météo France (the French national meteorological service), and concluded that the witness may have been an aircraft coming from Lyon and landing at Le Havre-Octeville airport, approaching the runway from the northeast, three-quarters facing a southerly wind. The radar tracks, however, do not show this aircraft, but these tracks are only recorded for an area less than 10 km west of Montivilliers; the aircraft coming from the Southeast must pass through the LHO aeronautical landmark, located at Mannevillette (LHO IAF 49°35'51.1" N - 0°00'10'51.8" E), well north of this track area: it will have bypassed, first to the East and then to the North, the area selected for the radar track (see attached map). A head-on aircraft at low altitude is visible from 20 km, or even 30 km and more depending on weather conditions; it appears as a single point of light, because the position lights and flashing lights, much less powerful than the narrow-beam landing lights, are not visible at this distance. On this day, excellent horizontal visibility of 60 km was noted, despite the heavy cloud cover. Météociel. These rare weather conditions may explain why witnesses do not usually notice this regular airliner. It is also possible that the pilot chose a particular route or altitude that day. The same aircraft, seen from the side, then displays its navigation lights (red or green depending on the side), and its flashing lights (red and/or white depending on the phase of flight), and the landing lights, directed towards the front of the aircraft, are almost no longer visible.">Météociel. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": very probable observation of an aircraft seen head-on, approaching Le Havre-Octeville.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon with colored flashes (green and red) in the night sky: probable sighting of a Civil Security helicopter.
description: On November 18, 2012, at approximately 8:30 p.m., a witness observed a light in the sky, first with the naked eye and then with binoculars. This light was stationary and flickered (green and red flashes); its center was black, and its intensity varied. The witness moved to the location, showed the light to several other people nearby, and then contacted the gendarmerie. A patrol was dispatched to the scene and also observed the phenomenon. The gendarmes alerted the Western Area Control Center (CRNA-O) near Brest, and the air traffic controller wrote a report indicating that a flight crew on approach to Quimper and he himself had not made any particular observations on that date. He also indicated that the military was not on duty in the area that evening and that the primary radars at Lanvéoc and Landivisiau had not detected anything unusual. Despite a neighborhood inquiry, only one witness statement was collected regarding this phenomenon. The witness observed a stationary glow in the sky for a long time, changing color, in a southeasterly direction: a fixed light in the sky suggests an astronomical phenomenon, and the color change could be due to scintillation. A light westerly wind and very humid conditions were noted that day. However, no bright celestial bodies were visible in that direction; on the other hand, the planet Jupiter was visible due east. The CNRA report provides additional information, such as the altitude of the UFO above the horizon and the fact that it was not detected visually or by radar by the crew of an aircraft approaching Quimper, nor by the primary radars at Lanvéoc and Landivisiau. The report also indicates the absence of military activity in the area. Considering the objective elements defined in the preceding chapters, we can conclude that this case should be classified as category B, indicating probable confusion with a helicopter. The phenomenon has all the characteristics of a helicopter observed at night, at a significant distance; possibly a Civil Security helicopter on a VFRn mission near Quimper Pluguffan Airport, corresponding to the azimuth of the observation. This testimony is of average quality (too concise, imprecise, and lacking essential data), and rather weak in its consistency, coming from a single witness and without a photograph. The observation is not unusual, as the UFO is easily identifiable, both in its appearance and its behavior. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of a Civil Security helicopter approaching Quimper Pluguffan Airport.

summary: Observation of the passage of a phenomenon illuminated by a green light and two red lights at the rear: lack of information.
description: On November 12, 2012, at 2:43 a.m., a witness observed an unidentified phenomenon passing across the sky for 20 seconds. No other witness statements were collected. The witness described a flying object as "a kind of flying car, lit up in green and equipped with red lights at the rear," moving at low altitude over the city. The object's trajectory and the red and green lights suggested a helicopter, but the witness did not mention any flashing lights or noise. The testimony was brief; GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group) repeatedly offered the witness an on-site meeting with an investigator, but the witness was unable to make themselves available. Due to this insufficient information, the case was classified as "C".

summary: Observation of the passage in the sky of a dark triangular phenomenon whose angles and center are marked by orange lights: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 30, 2015, GEIPAN received a questionnaire regarding an observation made on November 10, 2012, at 9:30 PM by a single witness. This witness, on their terrace, observed a dark triangular phenomenon in the sky, the corners and center of which were illuminated by yellow-orange lights. It moved slowly and silently, then rotated 90 degrees and headed due west at lightning speed. Based on the information gathered in the investigation report (see attached document), namely: - Yellow-orange color identical to that of lanterns. - Behavior identical to that of objects subjected to no or light winds. - Short observation duration (less than 1 minute), consistent with the lifespan of lanterns. - Date: a Saturday evening, consistent with the times when lanterns are typically released for celebrations. - Number consistent with the number of lanterns released. - Illusion of acceleration and disappearance caused by the lanterns going out. - 90° turn possibly caused by a horizontal shear phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this observation as a B-type case, a probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of an object with flashing red and white lights: probable observation of a light aircraft.
description: On November 5, 2012, at approximately 7:30 PM, two witnesses observed a bright red object with two flashing white hexagonal lights in the sky for one minute. Given the objective elements presented in the investigation report—namely, the observed lights and noise consistent with those of an aircraft, the trajectory along the axis of two nearby airfields during a takeoff or landing close to a light aircraft, and the existence of an airfield housing a flying club with light aircraft approved for night flights—we can conclude that the UFO observed by the witnesses was probably a light aircraft. This case is classified as a B-class sighting of a light aircraft shortly after takeoff or shortly before landing from or toward a nearby airfield.

summary: Observations of two luminous red-orange balls appearing successively in the sky and moving towards the sea: probable observations of the passage of two Thai lanterns.
description: On November 2, 2012, around 11:00 PM, three people were intrigued by the sighting of two red orbs of light in the sky, five minutes apart. These orbs moved slowly towards the sea and disappeared in an upward trajectory. This observation had all the characteristics of Thai lanterns: orange-red lights moving silently at low altitude, carried by the wind (see Météociel report: light northwesterly wind), on a weekend evening. The hazy appearance above the lanterns could be due to steam emitted from the heated, damp envelope, or to smoke produced by the burner. Although the witness did not confirm this hypothesis, GEIPAN classified this case as "B": probable observation of two Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent and slow passage of an orange ball in the sky; straight trajectory: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: Recent report of an earlier observation. On July 23, 2015, a witness reported an observation made on October 31, 2012. That day, at 7:50 PM, the witness was intrigued by the silent passage of an orange ball across the sky. The movement was quite slow and straight. He filmed his observation. No other reports were collected. The crossing of the sky by an orange ball in just a few minutes strongly suggests a Thai lantern, especially on the eve of a public holiday and on Halloween. The video, which was briefly publicly available on YouTube, is consistent with this scenario. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the passage of a bright cylindrical object in the sky with a red halo on one side; rapid disappearance: observation of the passage of an aircraft illuminated by the sun.
description: On October 28, 2012, around 10:00 AM, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon in the clear sky. From their balcony, looking west, the witness followed the slow movement of a bright, silvery, cylindrical object with a small red halo to its left. The witness went back inside to get their camera, but when they returned 15 seconds later, everything had disappeared. No noise or smoke was observed. Only one witness statement was recorded. The continuous red light (red halo) to the left of the "cigar" and the sun behind the witness are consistent with an aircraft illuminated by the sun. According to the witness's drawing, the angle of view of a fuselage (from the side) could explain the absence of visible wings. The duration of the observation (3 minutes) seems exaggerated. The witness's viewpoint (approximately 1/35th of a second) appears limited for such a long duration. The sky above the witness is crisscrossed by numerous contrails in all directions (the sky on Google Street View is full of condensation trails in this area). What makes the sight strange for the witness is the absence of wings and the rapid disappearance. What reduces the level of strangeness is the absence of other witnesses and the interruption of the observation. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Aircraft.

summary: Observation by a motorist through her windscreen of a white luminous phenomenon and its movements: lack of information.
description: On October 24, 2012, at 7:50 PM, a motorist noticed a bright light moving quickly across the sky. The witness described a bright white light that, on a downward trajectory, disappeared after a few seconds. The witness then discerned a shape, and the light gradually reappeared on an upward trajectory before disappearing completely behind the hill. No sound was heard. Only one witness account was collected. First, to try to answer one of the witness's questions (e.g., "I would like to know if other people have reported this phenomenon to you"), we searched for similar reports from the Grenoble area at the same time and date. Unfortunately, we found no results. Given the objective elements gathered in the attached investigation report—namely, that the physical and dynamic characteristics of the UFO are inconsistent with those of an airplane, helicopter, drone, or rocket, but that a reflection in the windshield could have caused the same scene—we cannot conclude on the nature of the observed UFO due to a lack of corroboration, other eyewitness accounts, or photographs. This eyewitness account is of average consistency: precise but brief (observation lasting 10 to 15 seconds), coming from a single witness traveling in a car, and without a photograph. The observation is moderately strange because it involves an object with unusual behavior and appearance, but which can be explained by conventional phenomena. This case is classified as C due to a lack of information.

summary: Successive observations of movement of colored luminous phenomena in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On October 13, 2012, at approximately 2:05 AM, a witness observed, within a very short period (8 to 10 seconds), to the west, at a distance of about ten meters, objects resembling pale blue shooting stars, very faint, following a short trajectory, crossing paths in all directions and quickly fading away. These UFOs were located at an estimated height of 4 or 5 fingers above the hills and rooftops of the village. Immediately afterward, the witness made a second observation, this time at the zenith, and for 15 to 20 seconds observed a bright red point moving westward like a satellite. This object then stopped abruptly for 3 or 4 seconds while its brightness increased rapidly, giving it a spherical appearance surrounded by a blurry red halo. Then it moved in a series of very rapid zigzags made up of sharp, angular turns, without any jolts or accelerations/decelerations, before resuming its initial trajectory, stopping a second time, emitting a series of vibrations, then stopping a third time before disappearing completely near the wind turbines at very high speed. No other eyewitness accounts were collected. The conclusion of the investigation report (see document) indicates that two observations were reported: - the UFOs observed initially exhibited behavior that could not be likened to that of shooting stars; - then the observation of another UFO whose behavior was unlike that of any known man-made or natural object; - the hypothesis of laser beams was rejected in the absence of cloud cover or haze. - The zigzag trajectory cannot be explained by a micro-nystagmus perception phenomenon. This observation cannot be explained with the available information. Therefore, to supplement or clarify these observations, GEIPAN requested a meeting with the witness at the observation site for an interview and reconstruction. Even two years later, this meeting could have been crucial. Despite several attempts by phone, voicemail, text message, and email, the witness could not be reached to schedule an appointment. A more recent attempt was unsuccessful. It was therefore not possible to make progress in the explanation, nor even to consolidate the consistency and reliability of the testimony, which remain insufficient given the level of strangeness of the observations described in the questionnaire. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: insufficient information.

summary: Observation of the rapid EO passage of a bright white point in the sky: lack of information.
description: On October 9, 2012, at 11:32 PM, two people observed a bright white point moving rapidly across a starry, dark sky. Only one eyewitness account was reported. The observation of a white point crossing the sky from east to west in a few seconds suggests a bolide (a large shooting star), that is, the entry of a meteoroid (meteorite) into the atmosphere. The absence of a trail is unusual. This event was not recorded in the BOAM (meteor observer database). The information provided is insufficient to confirm this bolide hypothesis, which nevertheless remains plausible (peak activity of Delta aurigid meteors on October 10). GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information. A similar observation was noted in Limoges 20 minutes earlier on the same day.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a white glow with a small bluish halo in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On October 9, 2012, between 11:00 PM and 11:30 PM, a witness in their garden observed a rapidly moving white glow with a small bluish halo in the partly cloudy sky. Five minutes later, the witness recognized it as a shooting star. The observation of a white point crossing the sky in a few seconds suggests a bolide (a large shooting star), that is, the entry of a meteoroid (meteorite) into the atmosphere. The absence of a trail is unusual. This event was not recorded in the BOAM (meteor observer database). The information provided is insufficient to validate this bolide hypothesis, which nevertheless remains plausible (peak activity of Delta aurigid meteors on October 10). GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information. On the same day, 20 minutes later, a similar observation was noted in Lieu-Saint-Amand (59).

summary: Observation of two luminous points stationary in the sky then moving rapidly: very likely observation of two aircraft during military maneuvers.
description: On Tuesday, October 9, 2012, at approximately 10:40 PM, a witness observed two dark yellow lights in the sky from their garden. These lights appeared stationary at first, then moved rapidly in a southwest direction. No unusual noises were heard during the three-minute observation. The witness then lost sight of the lights. After an on-site investigation with the witness and further inquiries with military authorities, it appears that the observation coincided perfectly with large-scale military maneuvers. However, the authorities did not specify the type of aircraft involved (helicopter, airplane, or lighting balloon). Furthermore, we have no other observations of the same phenomenon to confirm that it occurred over an airbase. In conclusion, we have a serious and well-supported hypothesis, but no formal proof. GEIPAN classifies this case in category B, very probable observation of two aircraft during military maneuvers.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a luminous orange object in the sky: lack of information.
description: On October 5, 2012, at 11:26 PM, a witness observed a luminous, orange, oval-shaped object with wings on each side moving silently in the sky for one minute. No other witness accounts were collected. Given the information gathered during the investigation, namely: - No information on the "exact" azimuth of appearance and disappearance. - No information on the angular altitudes of appearance and disappearance. - Absence of angular measurements. - No further details on estimates of the object's altitude, distance, and size. We can conclude that the lack of precision prevents us from favoring any hypothesis. This case is classified as C, meaning the observation of a phenomenon that cannot be identified in its current state, as the lack of information prevents us from establishing a firm opinion. This testimony is of weak substance: imprecise and lacking in detail, and moreover, it lacks crucial data necessary for the continuation of the study. It consists of a single eyewitness account and no photographic or video documentation. The observation is not unusual, as it could have been a completely ordinary object (e.g., a night bird illuminated by streetlights, a military aircraft with its lights off); therefore, GEIPAN did not deem a field investigation necessary to bolster the case file.

summary: Observation of the passage of a white ball with a white trail in the sky over Réunion; descending trajectory: observation of the passage of a bolide.
description: On October 1, 2012, at 7:35 PM, several witnesses observed a rapidly passing sphere with a white trail in the sky, which appeared to descend towards the ocean. A general power outage occurred very soon after the sphere's passage. Only one witness account was collected. The characteristics of the observation were entirely consistent with those of a fireball. The witness experienced a strange connection, associating the observation with the power outage, which was merely a coincidence (power outages are not uncommon in the region, and were even predicted for that week by EDF). The fireball could not be confirmed in the records (which are never exhaustive, especially outside of mainland France), but it remains the most likely hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: fireball

summary: Observation of the movement of a bright and flashing point: observation of a weather balloon.
description: On September 29, 2009, at 3:00 PM, a witness observed a small, bright white object flashing at high altitude through a window. After one minute, the object stopped moving and then resumed its trajectory without flashing. According to information gathered by telephone from the witness, he was looking south, and the object was moving east (see map). Ground weather reports indicated a northwesterly wind at 2:00 PM, then a northerly wind at 3:00 PM. Therefore, the observation does not correspond to a low-altitude, wind-borne object. However, Météo-France conducts daily weather balloon launches from Trappes around 12:00 UTC, or 2:00 PM local time, which is one hour before the observation (see the report which indicates that the surface wind was fairly light from the NW (5 kt) at 2:00 PM, then became stronger from the W (25 kt) above 2800 m, before returning to the NW at higher altitudes). Since the winds aloft were blowing eastward, this balloon would explain the observation, approximately one hour after the launch. The flashing corresponds to the rotation of the balloon or reflectors. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as identified by the observation of a Météo-France weather balloon launched from Trappes at 2:00 PM.

summary: Long observations of the silent passage of several dozen luminous spheres in the night sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, September 29, 2012, two witnesses observed the silent passage of thirty to forty luminous red-orange spheres in the night sky. They appeared spaced at regular intervals and moved in a straight line along the same north-south axis. They seemed to gather above the Château Charles forest in Montmarault. The witnesses decided to investigate, but found the spheres had disappeared. The information provided by the witnesses led the investigation toward the observation of Thai lanterns, which shared the same characteristics: an orange glow, moving silently in the wind. The description of the phenomenon corresponds to the physics of lanterns, illuminated by a candle. The candle generates the hot air that allows the lantern to rise into the sky, like a hot air balloon. As seen by the witness, it appears as an orange sphere (the lantern's envelope, the color of candlelight). The temperature being stable inside the lantern's envelope, and in the absence of wind gusts, it remains at a constant altitude. This phenomenon makes no noise. The weather situation in this region, according to Météociel, reports a north-south wind of 10 to 15 km/h, cloud cover 6/8, a temperature of 12°C, and a pressure of 1020 hPa. These floating objects were therefore being pushed from North to South, which corresponds to the trajectory of the phenomenon described by the witness and the police report. However, the witness's estimate of the lanterns' speed at 50 km/h is significantly overestimated. This is due to the inaccurate judgment of the distance of an unrecognized object. For the same angular velocity (the only element perceived by a witness), an overestimation of the distance leads to an overestimation of the speed. The date, Saturday evening, can also be considered, a time conducive to a festive gathering of family or friends. A wedding reception is mentioned in the police report. The successive lighting of the lanterns corresponds to the witness's description of lanterns following the same trajectory (direction of the wind), spaced 20 to 25 seconds apart. As for the grouping of all these spheres above the distant forest, this corresponds to a perspective effect, like train tracks that appear to converge on the horizon. Similarly, the observer's perception that the first spheres were waiting for the others is part of the same perspective effect. As for their disappearance, this corresponds to the end of the candle's combustion. Deprived of its heat source, the lantern, now invisible, falls. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this as an A sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of luminous phenomena in the form of white flashes behind a cloud and discovery of luminous balls on the film taken during the observation: observation of distant lightning before a storm.
description: On September 24th, around 12:45 AM, a witness observed a series of luminous phenomena in the sky, in the form of bright white flashes behind a large white cloud. These phenomena originated from the south and east, and the witness filmed these flashes for eight minutes using a "spy pen." No sound was heard. When the witness reviewed the video, he was surprised to see luminous orbs that he had not observed live. The witness's wife also observed the phenomenon, but only one witness statement was recorded. Lightning strike records show significant thunderstorm activity over the Nord-Pas-de-Calais region in the middle of the night (see Météociel). The witness confirms that there was a thunderstorm after 2:00 AM. The flashes observed behind the clouds originated from this storm activity. The video, taken with a small "spy pen," does not show these bright flashes, but rather stationary points of light. This type of camera is not very sensitive in low light, which may explain why distant lightning flashes behind the clouds were too faint to register on the sensor. The points of light appearing in the video are most likely stationary lights: streetlights or something similar. The witness did not see them with the naked eye. Since these spy cameras do not have a viewfinder, the witness cannot compare what he is filming with what he sees. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of distant lightning before a thunderstorm. The lights filmed in the video appear to be streetlights.

summary: Observations of several round, luminous objects appearing and disappearing in the cloudy sky: lack of information.
description: On September 23, 2012, at 5:05 PM, a driver and his partner observed several round, luminous objects appearing and disappearing in the clouds. No other reports were collected. The witnesses were driving south-southwest (see map). The weather forecast (see Meteociel report) indicated a strong southerly wind and fairly overcast skies in Clermont-Ferrand. The luminous objects seen by the witnesses could have been metallic balloons reflecting the sun. Because the wind was blowing in the opposite direction to the witnesses, they appeared almost stationary. The date and time of the observation are consistent with a balloon release following a festival or sporting event. Although this hypothesis is consistent with the witnesses' statements, GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) was unable to confirm it through further investigation. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information to validate the balloon hypothesis.

summary: Observations of the slow passage of a luminous phenomenon: atmospheric reentry of a bolide.
description: Several eyewitness accounts from pilots in flight and a ground witness describe the slow passage of a luminous phenomenon across the sky around midnight on the night of September 21-22, 2012. A single observation report, sent by the Eastern Regional Air Navigation Center (CRNA EST) in Reims, records the four pilots' accounts: all indicate direct observations of a luminous phenomenon under clear skies, with no radar echoes detected and no anomalies in the operation of flight instruments. One of the pilots specifies seeing a blue light. The ground witness describes a fluorescent green ball with a trail following a downward trajectory. This phenomenon, observed in northern France by four pilots in flight and a ground witness in Laon, was also widely observed from England, moving from east to west, and more slowly than typical meteors. Jeremie Vaubaillon, a meteor specialist at the Institute of Celestial Mechanics and Ephemeris Calculation, was consulted on this case: "We have strong reasons to believe that this object is very interesting. It could be a small asteroid temporarily captured by Earth." Given the pilots' northward viewing angle and that this type of phenomenon occurs between 100 and 60 km altitude, it is indeed the same phenomenon that was observed by the four pilots, the witness in Laon, and the witnesses in England. GEIPAN classifies this case as 'A': observation of a bolide: meteoroid reentry.

summary: Observation of two fixed luminous phenomena: astronomical observation of Venus and Jupiter.
description: On September 17, 2012, between 6:50 and 7:20 a.m., a witness was intrigued by the presence of two luminous phenomena in the sky. The witness took two photographs: one facing east and the other facing south. The witness undoubtedly observed the planet Jupiter, with a magnitude of -2.5 (that is, much brighter than the stars of Ursa Major, with a magnitude of 1.7), to the south, and saw the planet Venus, with a magnitude of -4.7 (that is, even brighter), to the east, which became invisible at sunrise. (See the corresponding star charts.) GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of Venus and Jupiter

summary: Observation of the presence of a black ball in the sky: probable observation of a balloon.
description: On September 17, 2012, at 2:20 PM, a witness noticed a black sphere in the sky that appeared stationary. The witness observed this seemingly motionless black object, quite low on the horizon. The witness circled it a quarter turn, which confirms the object's short distance and altitude. The north wind of 10 to 20 km/h (see report) seemed too weak to fly a kite. The spherical shape suggested a balloon. The cloud cover seemed unsuitable for a test of a thermal balloon (heated by the sun). It was probably a festive helium balloon, held by a tether (which would have been invisible beyond 100 meters) or floating in the light wind that day. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable balloon sighting.

summary: Observation of the SW-NE passage of a very bright, luminous yellow object, breaking into two pieces, descending trajectory: probable atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On September 16, 2012, at 10:16 PM, a witness observed a very bright yellow object coming from the southwest, moving rapidly towards the mountain above the horizon. The very bright object broke into two pieces that disappeared behind the horizon to the northeast. The witness's description perfectly matches the observation of a fireball with fragmentation, most likely caused by the reentry of a meteoroid into the atmosphere. This case is classified as "B".

summary: Brief observation of the silent movement of a bright point in the sky: probable observation of a bolide.
description: On September 16, 2012, at 8:24 PM, a witness on their balcony was drawn to the silent movement of a bright white point. Its trajectory was east-west, and the phenomenon disappeared behind the Jura Mountains. No sound was heard during the 4-second observation. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. Of moderate strangeness and good consistency (a single witness, but with a very precise account), this case appears to be a possible misidentification of a natural atmospheric reentry (a bolide, also called a meteor). Although the description of the UFO is entirely characteristic of a bolide, no other witness could be found to formally explain the case. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of their observation based on their experience (a short-duration observation in a twilight sky). This case is classified as Class B, probable observation of a bolide.

summary: Observation of the movement in the sky of a white ball resembling a cloud: lack of information.
description: On September 16, 2012, at 4:40 PM, a walker observed a white sphere resembling a cloud moving towards him, remaining high in the sky. As he approached, the object, estimated at one centimeter in diameter, increased in size to approximately three times its original volume. The witness took a photograph. GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) received his testimony in May 2013. GEIPAN analyzed the hypothesis of an object carried by the wind. Unfortunately, there is no weather station near Gondrecourt. Weather readings from Saint-Dizier (52), 45 km away, and Nancy-Essey (55 km away) show extremely variable wind speeds, both in direction (NE, SW, S, SE) and speed (4 to 25 km/h). It is therefore impossible to definitively state that this object was carried by the wind, although it is highly probable. The change in brightness of the object from the zenith, where it appears white in the photo, to the horizon, where it appears gray, suggests a fairly low-lying object rather than a cloud. Furthermore, the witness clearly saw the object grow larger throughout the observation, which supports the hypothesis of a very low-altitude object. If the object were at an altitude of 100 meters, a 12 km/h wind would have carried it across half the sky (the 90th parallel) in one minute, traveling 200 meters. The described shape could be consistent with a ball of down, perhaps carried from a nest or a swarm of insects. These are only hypotheses and cannot be confirmed. Due to the lack of local wind data and the inability to estimate the object's altitude, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C": lack of precise information to give a consolidated opinion.

summary: Observations of successive and silent passages of white luminous points in the night sky: probable observations of Thai lanterns.
description: Recent report of an earlier observation. In May 2015, GEIPAN received a report of an observation made on September 16, 2012. That evening, around 11:30 PM, a witness observed the silent passage of several white lights across the sky. The witness observed this three times, the lights always following the same path. No other reports were collected. The observation of luminous orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby during a private party. The witness's video also shows the lanterns disappearing one after another, which is also typical (burner burnout). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of several yellow-orange luminous points: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, September 15, 2012, around 11:00 PM, several people observed the silent movement of several yellow-orange lights in the sky, which gradually faded. Only one person reported the sighting. The witness's description (yellow lights, gradually fading into a black shape, slow horizontal movement) is entirely characteristic of a Thae lantern sighting. The coincidence with the fireworks display on a Saturday night is also a contributing factor. The very light wind, blowing from the southwest, is not inconsistent with this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable Thae lantern (flying lantern) sighting.

summary: Observation of multiple multicolored points forming a stationary trapezoid in the sky: lack of information.
description: On September 15, 2012, at 10:30 PM, a witness observed multiple multicolored points of light, forming a trapezoidal shape, from their open bathroom window. The points were not flashing. The shape appeared stationary, the size of a large building. Its height was compared to that of a helicopter in flight. The witness took some photos. The UFO disappeared as the witness looked away. The strangeness of the phenomenon can be considered low (static, persistent, and dimly lit), with a possible explanation but no confirmation. The testimony is of average consistency: a single witness and no correlation between what is visible in the photographs and the witness's description of the phenomenon. Furthermore, the investigation took place long after the observation. GEIPAN classifies this case as category C due to a lack of corroborating information (other witnesses, good-quality photographs, reports of animations). The most likely hypothesis, the observation of a light projection-type manifestation, could not be confirmed.

summary: Observation in the sky of the movement of an elongated object of blue/purple color: probable observation of a festive balloon.
description: On September 15, 2012, at approximately 1:35 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent SSE-NNE movement of an elongated, colored object in the sky. An amateur photographer, he instinctively took two pictures. With a moderate southeast to east wind (see Meteociel report for Nice), the witness observed and photographed a complex-shaped, violet-blue flying object to the southeast. The object's movement was consistent with the wind direction, and its appearance resembled a silver (Mylar) helium-filled party balloon. The witness, standing on his balcony facing the wind, was unable to accurately determine the wind direction. GEIPAN classified this case as "B": probable observation of a party balloon.

summary: Observation of a fixed object of triangular shape, blue in color surrounded by bright points; sudden disappearance in the sky: lack of information.
description: On September 14, 2012, at approximately 6:25 a.m., a witness observed a blue, triangular object with bright spots in the sky for about five seconds. The stationary object appeared to suddenly fall and then abruptly disappeared. No other witness accounts were collected. This observation differs from the most common misinterpretations: - the star chart reveals no significant celestial bodies to the west that could have caused an illusion; - the hypothesis of a satellite or constellation of satellites has also been ruled out due to the absence of corresponding objects listed on the Calsky website; - at this very early hour, the hypothesis of a drone or recreational aircraft seems extremely unlikely; - the description of the phenomenon is very different from that of an airplane, although it is possible that an airplane was within the witness's field of vision at that time and in that direction. The Météociel weather report for Toulouse-Blagnac indicates a strong westerly wind. It is above Montgiscard that aircraft preparing to land at Blagnac line up along the northwest axis of the Blagnac runway: an aircraft approaching head-on, before its turn to the northwest, could have appeared as a series of bright points, visible only before the turn to the northwest (see map). This latter hypothesis, bordering on the implausible and too tenuous, is not retained as it is not confirmed by other corroborating evidence (air traffic reports, photos, other witnesses). GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of corroborating evidence.

summary: Observation by a motorist of three flashing lights moving at low altitude and forming a triangle: probable sighting of an aircraft.
description: On September 12, 2012, at approximately 9:30 PM, a motorist was intrigued by the presence of three colored lights (red, blue, and white) in the sky at low altitude. These lights flashed and formed a triangular shape. No unusual noise was heard as the phenomenon moved, changed direction, and disappeared in the direction of Saussenac. The observation lasted two minutes. No other witness statements were collected. Given its moderate strangeness and limited consistency (single witness, short observation duration), this case appears to be a possible case of mistaken identity involving an aircraft (see the investigation report). However, despite a fairly typical description, the poor quality of the witness statement and the lengthy processing time prevented the formal identification of any aircraft. The issue was not the witness's visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their own experience (fatigue, night driving). This case is class B, probable observation of an aircraft.

summary: Observations from a boat of three aligned and inclined red lights; sudden extinction: lack of information.
description: On September 11, 2012, between midnight and 2:00 a.m., two people aboard a sailboat approaching the port of Île d'Yeu observed three red lights, aligned and angled above the ocean, to the right of the green buoy at the port entrance. The phenomenon remained stationary for several minutes and made no sound before disappearing abruptly. The two witnesses then continued their maneuvers to enter the port. The observation of three red orbs at low altitude, almost stationary for three to four minutes, suggests the presence of Thai lanterns. The local wind recorded at St. Sauveur (see weather report) indicated a light southwesterly wind: the witnesses would have liked to see a slight movement to their right; however, the witnesses were themselves moving, and the port of Joinville (on the northwest side of the island) is sheltered from southwesterly winds. Thai lanterns are most often licked after parties on Saturday nights; the sighting occurred on a Tuesday around 1 a.m., but in a very touristy area. The simultaneous extinguishing of all three lights is highly unlikely for lanterns. Given these three factors that preclude the Thai lantern hypothesis, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration. The report was submitted to GEIPAN too late for an investigation to be conducted with air traffic control.

summary: Observation of the passage of an orange luminous phenomenon with a long tail at very high altitude: lack of information.
description: On September 10, 2012, at approximately 8:20 PM, two witnesses observed the slow passage at very high altitude of a luminous orange phenomenon with a long tail. Its trajectory was straight. It disappeared southward, hidden by a cloud. Only one witness briefly reported their observation. This somewhat unusual distant sighting is poorly documented and imprecise; the description suggests an aircraft contrail visible through low clouds. The orange color is common for contrails located to the west at sunset (8:13 PM that day at that location). Nevertheless, GEIPAN (the French National Observatory of Explosive Ordnance Disorder) does not have enough concrete evidence to support this hypothesis. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Brief observation of an intense white-orange light in the sky: probable observation of a flash from the satellite to ISIS 1 e.
description: On September 10, 2012, at 10:25 PM, a witness briefly observed a very bright, orange-white phenomenon in the sky. This intense light disappeared abruptly. The witness noticed no noise. Only one witness account of this phenomenon was recorded. Considering the objective elements defined in the investigation report (see document), namely the duration of the observation, consistent with that of satellite flashes (approximately 20 seconds), the appearance of a very bright flash, its elongated shape moving slowly horizontally, and its position in the sky (azimuth and altitude), consistent with that of the ISIS 1 satellite, which was recorded and visible at the date and time of the observation, we can conclude that this case likely concerns the observation of a flash from the ISIS 1 satellite as it exited the Earth's shadow. This case is classified as B, as a probable observation of a flash from the ISIS 1 satellite. Uncertainty remains regarding the identity of the satellite that originated the phenomenon.

summary: Several witnesses observed the random movements of two lights of different intensities: astronomical observations of Jupiter and Aldebaran with autokinetic illusion.
description: On September 9, 2012, around midnight, a group of three friends were observing shooting stars and were intrigued by a bright star that appeared to move quite rapidly in all directions, followed by another, fainter light. Only one witness account was recorded. The star chart shows the planet Jupiter and the star Aldebaran in the position described by the witnesses. The movements of these points of light, as described by the witnesses, are clearly inconsistent with the hypothesis of observing fixed celestial bodies. The hypothesis of an autokinetic illusion was put forward to explain this account: this area of the sky is sparsely populated with other bright stars, making this hypothesis plausible. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of Jupiter and Aldebaran, probably observed with an autokinetic illusion.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of two bright red lights: probable observation of Thai lanterns
description: On September 8, 2012, at 11:00 PM, two people observed the slow and silent passage of two round, red, luminous objects. One of the objects moved in a different direction from the first and suddenly disappeared. The description of the phenomenon and the photograph strongly suggest Thai lanterns: red-orange orbs moving slowly for a few minutes. The movement from south to north or northwest is consistent with the very light, unstable wind, blowing mostly from the south. Saturday evenings are the preferred times for lantern licking. The disappearance of the objects simply corresponds to the extinction of the flame due to the depletion of the paraffin. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent passage of an object in the sky: probably a helicopter at low altitude.
description: On September 7, 2012, at 9:00 PM, a group of four people observed a bright point of light moving slowly and silently in their direction in the dark sky. Upon changing their course, the witnesses observed a dark, rounded shape. Only one witness statement was recorded. This observation of a bright point of light low on the horizon suggested a low-flying aircraft. An investigation was requested from military air traffic control: the radar data (attached) indicates low-altitude air traffic between 9:23 PM and 9:25 PM (times indicated on the radar record are in Universal Time) in the direction of the witness's observation, between Morangis and Brugny, coming from the west, in an area without an airfield. The low altitude and winding flight path suggest that a helicopter was operating in that area. However, the witness observed the object between 9:00 PM and 9:10 PM, and it was moving west, while radar tracks indicate a westward trajectory. These tracks therefore do not correspond to the observation, but they do demonstrate aerial activity in the area. It is possible that similar activity occurred 20 minutes earlier (rotation), but at too low an altitude to be detected by radar. Radar tracks begin at 9:00 PM. If the observation took place shortly before 9:00 PM, the aerial activity would not have been recorded at that time. The silence observed during the observation is not surprising for a helicopter seen at a distance of 10 km. Given this information and these uncertainties, GEIPAN classifies this relatively unfamiliar case as a Category B observation of a helicopter. The low degree of unusualness of the phenomenon does not warrant a field investigation.

summary: Observation of the evolutions of a set of fixed lights outlining a circular shape: probable observation of Skyrose-type light animation.
description: On September 2, 2012, at 4:00 AM, several people observed a circular shape in the cloudy sky, estimated to be between 50 and 100 meters in diameter. It moved silently at low altitude and contained about fifteen fixed lights. The object rotated on its axis. The lights suddenly went out, and the shape disappeared. Only one witness account was recorded. This report of observing rotating circular lights (see the witness's drawing) strongly resembles the light shows used in nightclubs. A nightclub in Cazères (31) or Martres (31) often uses this type of display. What surprised the witness was the absence of an upward beam, but this is only visible in humid weather: the weather forecast for that day (at Toulouse-Blagnac Airport) indicated relatively dry air (50% humidity) and a total cloud ceiling (8/8), providing ideal conditions for the best effect from this type of projector. The end of the observation, around 4:20 a.m. on Sunday, coincides with the closing time of nightclubs. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of a Skyrose-type light display.

summary: Long observation of the silent movements of a luminous yellow circle in the cloudy sky: probable observation of a laser animation.
description: On September 1, 2012, a witness was intrigued by the silent, horizontal movements of a luminous yellow circle in the cloudy sky. The observation lasted nearly half an hour. No other witnesses reported seeing the phenomenon. The description of the event (a yellow circle appearing and disappearing in the clouds) suggests a disco spotlight; Saturday night is a prime time for this type of display. The police investigation found no evidence of any nearby establishment that might have staged such an event, but it is sometimes visible from over 10 km away. GEIPAN classifies this unusual case as category "B": probable observation of a luminous display.

summary: Observation and photography of a luminous phenomenon low on the horizon: confirmed observation of a parhelion.
description: 2012 UFO sighting was reported to GEIPAN in 2015. On August 31, 2012, a passenger in a car traveling from Chartres (28) to Caen (14) was intrigued by the presence of a very bright, yellow-yellow phenomenon low on the horizon, which he could not explain. The phenomenon appeared to be moving, as did the witnesses. The witness took a photograph. Only one questionnaire was collected, but the driver also saw the luminous phenomenon. The location of the sighting or the road was not precisely indicated by the witness, nor was it defined by the investigation. Based on the information gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - the appearance, brightness, and color of the UFO; - the sun low on the horizon and the UFO at the same altitude; - the presence of clouds conducive to the formation of a parhelion; - the presence of a trail characteristic of a parhelion. -The angular distance separating the sun from the UAP is consistent with that of the small halo of a parhelion. GEIPAN concludes that the UAP observed by the witnesses is very likely a parhelion phenomenon. The case is classified as a confirmed observation of a parhelion.

summary: Observation of the passage of a bright light in the constellation of Orion: probable observation from the Chinese space station Tiangong1.
description: A witness observed the sky, specifically the constellation Orion, on August 29, 2012, at 6:00 AM. For approximately five seconds, he saw a bright light cross the upper part of Orion, then continue in a straight line before gradually disappearing towards the northeast. A check of satellite passes (see Calsky record) showed the Chinese space station Tiangong-1 passing at that moment, moving from west to east, very bright, and slightly above Orion (see sky chart). Since the witness indicated a southwest to northeast trajectory, GEIPAN classified this case as "B": probable observation of the Chinese space station Tiangong-1.

summary: Observation of the movements of a white and green luminous phenomenon in the sky: lack of information.
description: On August 27, 2012, at 10:00 PM, a motorist and his passengers were intrigued by the presence of a moving white and green luminous phenomenon in the sky. Only one eyewitness account was reported. This very brief account, describing a very fast-moving green phenomenon, had some characteristics of a bolide (meteorite impact). However, the account was too vague, despite a request for information from GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of the Phenomena of Paris), to confirm this hypothesis. GEIPAN classified this case as "C" due to the lack of consistency in the eyewitness testimony.

summary: Short observation of the rapid and silent movement of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of the atmospheric reentry of a natural meteor (bolide).
description: On Sunday, August 26, 2012, at 10:07 PM, a witness was intrigued by the rapid and silent passage of a white luminous phenomenon across the sky. Only one questionnaire was received, but other witnesses in southwestern France sent emails to GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimental and Astronomical Research). This very brief observation of a luminous ball crossing part of the sky in one second suggests an atmospheric reentry of a natural meteor, a phenomenon known as a bolide. GEIPAN received three other simultaneous reports in southwestern France: in Agen (47), Toulouse (31), and Martel (46). The Futura-Sciences website also recorded several observations of the bolide: Futura-sciences. It is worth remembering that these phenomena occur at very high altitudes (from 80 km to 30 km) and are therefore visible from the ground over an area approximately 500 km in diameter. They are always perceived as close by witnesses (see A fireball?). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of a fireball: atmospheric reentry of a natural meteor.

summary: Observation by a witness of the silent movement in the sky of several dozen red objects on a north-south trajectory and at constant speed: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 26, 2012, at approximately 12:40 AM, a witness observed and photographed a luminous phenomenon in the sky that intrigued him: several dozen red, non-flashing objects moved silently along a north-south trajectory. They all followed each other at a regular distance and constant speed. The observation lasted about 5 minutes. The witness's description immediately suggested Thai lanterns: a horizontal passage of red orbs, in groups, without noise. The wind was blowing from the north at 11:00 PM, then from the northeast at midnight, which is consistent with the observed north-south movement. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of several waves of luminous objects in the sky moving silently: probable observations of Thai lantern passages.
description: witness reported an observation made by several people on August 26, 2012, at 9:30 PM: 12 objects moved silently westward. These objects appeared in waves. They were described as having an ovoid shape with a red rim, an orange interior, and three clearly visible yellow spheres inside. The witness filed a report with the gendarmerie, which will conduct an investigation. The local press will also be contacted. The color of the objects, their slow movement in the light easterly wind (see map and weather report), and their release in series are characteristic of sky lantern releases. Detailed photographic analysis showed that the light emitted by the objects was very similar to that emitted by Thai lanterns (see photographic analysis). However, these objects were not circular or elliptical like ordinary lanterns, but rather composed of three yellow dots within a red-orange envelope. Three Thai lanterns tied together would have the same appearance. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns tied together in threes.

summary: Observation of circular movements of an oval glow in the cloudy sky for thirty minutes: probable observation of a light animation.
description: On August 24, 2012, at 11:45 PM, a witness observed an oval-shaped light rotating in a circle in the cloudy sky for at least 30 minutes. This observation, on a Saturday night, suggests a projector used for nightclub entertainment. However, a nightclub in Bourgoin-Jallieu stated that it does not use this type of device. The use of such systems only 20 km from Lyon-Saint Exupéry Airport is also surprising. Despite these reservations, given that there are mobile projectors of this type available for rent, and that they can be seen from over 10 km away, this hypothesis remains the most likely. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a light show.

summary: Observation of the slow horizontal movement of a yellow glow in the sky: observation of the ISS.
description: On August 23, 2012, at 11:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a peculiar bright point in the sky. The witness then observed the slow horizontal movement of this yellow glow. No unusual noise was heard during the observation. The point disappeared, hidden by the urban landscape. After several exchanges with the witness, the direction of observation was precisely determined. This direction corresponds exactly to a pass of the International Space Station (ISS) above the southwest horizon at the same time (see Calsky record, magnitude -1.6). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation of the silent South-North movement of a rectangular object above the houses: probable sighting of a kite.
description: On August 23, 2012, at approximately 9:15 PM, three people observed a dark, rectangular object moving slowly from south to north in the sky above their homes. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted about three minutes. No other reports of this phenomenon were submitted to GEIPAN. According to the in-depth investigation, detailed in the attached report, the prevailing hypothesis is that these individuals likely saw a kite. The owner and their kite have not been found to date. This case is classified as "B".

summary: Observation of the passage of a point of light along a straight trajectory then with jerky movements: observation of the passage of the ISS with autokinetic illusion.
description: witness is intrigued by an observation made on August 22, 2012, at 10:19 PM. He observed the passage of a point of light which, after initially following a straight trajectory, made jerky movements from right to left before disappearing. The witness's description corresponds (appearance and direction of movement) to within one minute of the observation of the International Space Station passing overhead. The temporary disappearance corresponds to variations in the reflection of the sun on the station during its rotation. The jerky movements from right to left are a perceptual illusion called the "autokinetic illusion." (See pages 26 and 30 in /typo3conf/ext/dam_frontend/pushfile.php?docID=9932; this illusion occurs when the point of light being tracked is no longer surrounded by fixed reference points, for example when it crosses an area of the sky without very bright stars. This case is class "A": observation of the International Space Station ISS, with autokinetic illusion.

summary: Observations of the slow and silent passage of a large luminous ball: the ISS passing by.
description: On August 22, 2012, at 10:18 PM, a family was gazing at the starry sky. They were intrigued by the slow, silent passage of a luminous sphere whose intensity diminished before disappearing. The witnesses' description perfectly matches the observation of the International Space Station (ISS) (see Calsky document - ISS passage). In the second document (Calsky - sky chart), the white spheres represent the successive positions of the ISS against a background of stars; the spheres are larger the brighter the ISS appears. It is observed that at the beginning of the passage, the apparent movement of the ISS is small and that, moving eastward, the station entered the Earth's shadow. It is no longer illuminated by the sun and becomes invisible to observers. This case is classified as "A": observation of the passage of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation of the movement and then the rapid departure of a very bright white point in the sky: observation of the passage of the International Space Station.
description: On the evening of August 22, 2012, witnesses from their terrace observed a very bright point moving across the sky. The object moved strangely and at high speed. It appeared to be coming from the west and disappeared to the east. The Calsky website indicates a close pass of the International Space Station (ISS), extremely bright, visible from Brue-Auriac from 10:11 PM west to 10:17 PM southeast (see attached). The appearance of the ISS matches the witnesses' account. Its disappearance from view corresponds to its entry into Earth's shadow. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": ISS sighting.

summary: Observations of the silent and parallel passage across the horizon of a luminous orange object with halo and slight trail: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry.
description: On August 20, 2012, between 10 PM and 11 PM, two witnesses observed a very bright orange object passing silently in the north-south direction. Through binoculars, the witnesses could distinguish a halo and a faint trail. The observation lasted less than a minute before the object's brightness diminished and it was obscured by a nearby house. Only one witness reported their observation. The wind recorded in Bele was blowing lightly from the south to west, which makes a wind-borne object (e.g., a lantern) inconsistent. The duration of the observation (one minute), the trail observed through binoculars, the decrease in brightness, and the transition to white are consistent with the observation of a satellite debris fall. The Space-Track website mentions three debris falls that day, but the orbits do not correspond to the observation. Estimating the distance of this type of phenomenon is impossible for a witness. Given the precision of the testimony, despite the absence of proof, GEIPAN classifies this somewhat strange case "B": probable observation of atmospheric reentry: natural meteor or more likely satellite debris.

summary: Observations of the peculiar and silent movements of a round luminous object in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a luminous balloon.
description: On August 20, 2012, at approximately 10:30 PM, two witnesses observed the unusual and silent movements of a round, luminous object in the sky. It quickly disappeared. The weather report for Béziers Cap d'Agde (very close to Mèze) for that evening showed a light and very unstable wind, initially from the west, then shifting to the north. The movements of the object observed by the witnesses were clearly those of an object carried by the wind. Given the fireworks display that evening, it is possible that the object was a Thai lantern or other illuminated balloon launched for the festivities. The witness noted a white light, whereas witnesses of Thai lanterns most often describe orange-red lights. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," indicating a probable observation of an illuminated balloon (LED balloon).

summary: Observation in the sky of the sudden appearance of a luminous colored phenomenon: lack of information.
description: On August 19, 2012, between 1:10 AM (QT) and 1:21 AM (email), a witness observed a luminous colored phenomenon in the sky that intrigued them. No other reports were collected. Of moderate strangeness but weak consistency (single witness, brief testimony, contradictions, short observation, excessive interpretation), this case is too incomplete to be classified. Thus, it is unclear whether the UFO was observed near the horizon or in the open sky. The duration of the observation phases is also questionable, as they are sometimes described as lasting several minutes, and sometimes as being separated by only a few seconds (see the investigation report). The description of the observation is therefore too incomplete to be properly analyzed. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of bright points of light in the sky moving: probable sighting of an airplane.
description: On Sunday, August 19, 2012, at 8:30 PM, a witness was intrigued by the movement of two bright points in the sky.
