Given the objective evidence gathered during the investigation—namely, that the initial behavior of the UFOs resembled that of observed aircraft moving along the witness's line of sight, that the color and brightness of the UFOs were similar to the landing lights of airliners, and that the area overflown is frequently used by all kinds of civilian and military aircraft and is located near airports—the witness likely observed an aircraft. However, the final behavior of the first UFO, at a right angle to the sky, is, in the context of an observation at the zenith, a priori incompatible with that of such aircraft. But this is a common perceptual illusion observed with all moving bright points that disappear at night. At the time the investigation was conducted, GEIPAN no longer had access to aeronautical data to formally verify this hypothesis. This case is classified as B: probable sighting of an aircraft.

summary: Observation through binoculars of the zigzag movement of a bright point in the sky: probable observation of an airplane, with a perceptual illusion (flashing lights and autokinesis).
description: On August 17, 2012, at 11:35 PM, a person observing the sky with binoculars saw a bright point of light moving in a zigzag pattern and flashing irregularly. The testimony was recorded in November 2013. Astronautical verification indicated two satellites following a similar trajectory: Cosmos 2322 and 2360; however, they were of low luminosity. The flashing lights certainly suggested an airplane, but the zigzag path seemed inconsistent with this hypothesis. This area is frequently overflown by airliners on a North/South axis: the probability of an airplane on this trajectory is very high. The zigzag pattern is certainly surprising, but this illusion is not uncommon: for aircraft, if the anti-collision lights are synchronized and opposite, the witness interprets the alternating flashing of two distant lights as a zigzag. Furthermore, the autokinetic illusion (see: The perception of the movement of a point of light in the sky) can be added to this effect. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of an aircraft, with a perceptual illusion (flashing lights and autokinetic illusion).

summary: Observation of 3 colored and flashing lights moving in the night sky: probable sighting of a helicopter or a light aircraft in VFR night flight.
description: On August 15, 2012, around 10 p.m., a witness on a terrace was stargazing. He was intrigued by the unusual movement of two, then three, flashing colored lights. The witness moved to a different observation point. After considering various hypotheses about known phenomena, none satisfied him. His observation was confirmed by two other family members who suggested it might be a helicopter or a satellite. During the 15-minute observation, no noise was heard. The UFO disappeared from the witness's field of vision. No further witness statements were collected. Based on the evidence gathered during the investigation, namely the analysis of six hypotheses, two of which are highly consistent with the observation in terms of physical and dynamic characteristics (see the investigation report), GEIPAN classifies this case as Category B, indicating a probable sighting of a helicopter or light aircraft flying VFR at night towards Nantes Airport, Ancenis Airfield, or the Saint-Nazaire Air Base. This testimony is of average quality and consistency because, although three witnesses were present, only one completed the questionnaire, the other two providing only very brief answers to the gendarmes. Furthermore, the testimony is not accompanied by any photographs. Ultimately, the sighting is not particularly unusual, as the unidentified flying object (UFO) is easily identifiable, both in its appearance and its behavior.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a luminous object: probable observation of a festive balloon.
description: On August 14, 2012, at noon, a motorist noticed a luminous object in the sky that intrigued him. According to the witness, the object appeared to have articulated wings and flashing lights. He filmed the phenomenon and called his wife, who also saw the object in the sky. A third witness also saw the UFO. Witness T1's testimony is very precise and reliable. The observation lasted approximately three minutes. The three witnesses did not describe exactly the same thing, which may seem perfectly normal for witnesses T2 and T3, who saw the UFO quite far away and at different times. There is therefore no doubt about the reality of this phenomenon, which has all the characteristics of a helium-filled party balloon that may have escaped its owner's control. GEIPAN classifies this case as B, probable observation of a festive balloon inflated with helium.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of an orange light: lack of information.
description: On August 14, 2012, between 11:30 PM and 11:35 PM, a witness saw an orange light, round in shape and vaguely triangular, appear in the sky. He observed a silent movement: the trajectory was perfectly straight, constant, and horizontal. Three other witnesses saw the phenomenon but did not provide their accounts. The observation lasted approximately two minutes. Given the witness's description and the fact that it was a traditional holiday, the hypothesis of a Thai lantern was initially considered. However, the weather report from Avignon indicated a light southerly wind, seemingly incompatible with a northeasterly flow in the Methamis Valley. This hypothesis was therefore ruled out. The hypothesis of atmospheric reentry of satellite debris is ruled out due to the westward movement. The object's apparent speed is deemed too slow for a bolide (meteorite reentry), which is described as faint. Its appearance is also inconsistent with that of an aircraft. Given these various uncertainties, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C": lack of information.

summary: Long observation of the evolution of luminous disks in the cloudy sky: probable observation of a luminous animation.
description: On August 13, 2012, at 5:00 AM, a witness leaving his home was intrigued by the sight of a white luminous phenomenon in the cloud cover. A large circle formed by smaller circles appeared cyclically and rotated, changing direction. No sound was heard. The observation lasted 20 minutes at the scene, after which the witness got into his vehicle and continued to observe the phenomenon while driving. The phenomenon observed by the witness resembled a light show of this type: laser show (the "upward" beam is visible here because the observer is close to the projector; a distant observer would only see the luminous discs on the clouds). This show is not surprising in this area during peak tourist season, even at this early hour when nightclubs are still open. The presence of the "Asiana" nightclub is noted in the witness's direction of observation (West). The weather conditions (overcast skies 8/8, see report) are entirely favorable for the use of these devices. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a light display.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a red-orange ball: probable observation of the Thai lantern.
description: On August 13, 2012, at 12:09 AM, a witness observed from their window the silent passage of a luminous red-orange sphere across the sky, which disappeared behind the clouds after following a peculiar trajectory. Because the witness indicated their direction of observation very precisely, the map reconstruction is accurate (see map). The southwest direction of observation is, approximately, the direction of the light northeast wind: the witness therefore had the wind at their back. A flying object carried by the wind would then appear to move very little laterally; this is the hypothesis that was retained. The color of the described object resembles a Thai lantern, which could have been released at the end of a small private party, common during these summer evenings. However, the observation duration, estimated at 20 or 30 seconds, seems short. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent low-altitude passage of a dark object with three luminous circles at each end: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On the night of August 11-12, 2012, at approximately 12:25 a.m., a witness observed an object moving westward at low altitude while observing Cassiopeia. As it approached the roof of a building, the object became more visible. The witness described it as dark with bright, white circles at three points, forming the points of a triangle. The object moved silently and passed over the roof, obscuring it from the witness's view. Only one witness statement was recorded. The white lights, seen in isolation, strongly suggest Thai lanterns carried by the wind: - the direction of movement indicated by the witness is that of the wind that evening (see the website Infoclimat). - the fact that this occurred on a weekend night (in August!) conducive to festive events (lantern licking) reinforces this hypothesis. - the witness describes a lesser-known characteristic of these lantern lights: below the vertical, the light is not full because the underside of the lantern is a dark or black disc (see this video) and this is consistent with the description ("The perimeter of these three circles was luminous...while the center was dark, almost as dark as the color of the object." The witness writes of having seen a triangular object but specifies this: "Dark color barely standing out against that of the night sky. Little contrast between the object and the sky because it was dark." He also describes the lights placed at the extremities of the triangle: "Under the triangular object, a round shape (a circle) was located at each of the three extremities (points of the triangle)." This is very likely a classic case of misinterpretation (numerous GEIPAN reports of triangles and polygons caused by Thai lanterns), known as false form perception. The eye fills the space between the isolated points of light with a familiar shape that it believes it sees (Gestalt psychology). Once this pattern With this mental framework in place, this triangle can also be perceived as having a certain thickness ("Its edges seemed quite wide, thick"), simply because the lights of Thai lanterns also have a certain thickness in height (cylindrical objects). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of bright elements in the sky with trails: probable observation of aircraft and condensation trails.
description: Two people at their usual fishing spot were intrigued by the presence in the clear sky of bright, stationary or rapidly moving, silent objects followed by contrails. One person filmed and photographed the phenomena and then reported their observation. The photos and videos clearly suggested contrails. It was noted that, that morning, with the air likely being very dry and in the early morning light, these contrails appeared very bright and gave a particular impression of speed. GEIPAN classified this case as "A": observation of contrails from aircraft.

summary: Successive observations of the slow movement of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: passage of the ISS.
description: A witness was intrigued by the slow movements of a very bright phenomenon in the sky. He made these observations on the evenings of August 8 and 9, 2012. The witness's description and the times of the sightings are entirely consistent with observations of the International Space Station (ISS) passes on the evenings of August 8 and 9, 2012 (see the Calsky records of ISS passes on August 8 from 9:31 PM to 9:40 PM and then from 11:06 PM to 11:15 PM, and on August 9 from 10:13 PM to 10:24 PM and then from 11:50 PM to 11:57 PM), which should be compared to the dates and times of the observations (around 10:30 PM and 11:30 PM). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of two successive passes of the International Space Station (ISS) on two consecutive evenings.

summary: Observation of a second of the passage of a pale green light and a yellow/white triangle: lack of information.
description: This very brief observation (one second) of a somewhat unusual phenomenon (a bright light near the horizon at 6:15 a.m. sunrise) could have multiple origins: reflections of the sun on a satellite or aircraft, or a bolide (meteorite impact). GEIPAN classifies this as case "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Long observation of an object that was initially bright and orange, then circular and dark in the sky: probable observation of the sun's reflection on an airplane.
description: On Wednesday, August 8, 2012, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of an orange light in the sky. This light suddenly disappeared, and the witness then observed a dark, circular object that abruptly changed trajectory. The object disappeared into the urban landscape. The observation of an orange light in the sky 10 minutes after sunset (9:17 PM) strongly suggests the reflection of the sun on an aircraft (see the attached GEIPAN example). Aircraft are numerous in the Paris region at this time. The disappearance of the light corresponds to the aircraft passing into shadow. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of the sun's reflection on an aircraft.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear movement of a white-grey luminous point in the sky: probable observation of a balloon.
description: On August 8, 2012, at 11:45 AM, a witness and those around them observed a white-gray point moving in a straight line across the sky at a constant speed for 15 seconds. No trail was seen. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness, looking south, saw an object move from their left to their right, that is, from east to west. They observed the apparent size of this object decreasing as it passed. This account suggests the passage of a balloon of indeterminate shape, probably at a very low altitude because its apparent size diminished rapidly. The weather report from Limoges indicated an east to northwest wind at that time, which is consistent with this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a recreational balloon, a thermal balloon, or a helium-filled balloon.

summary: Observation in the sky of several black shapes appearing to fall while floating: probable observation of light and disparate debris carried by the wind.
description: On Wednesday, August 8, 2014, at approximately 2:40 PM, several people observed numerous black shapes moving in the clear sky. These shapes appeared to float and fall. One witness managed to take photographs and two videos of the objects, which at times appeared frayed. The observation lasted five minutes without any unusual noises being heard. Only one witness statement was recorded. This statement was very consistent: precise and accompanied by photographic and video evidence, but it came from a single witness. Considering the objective elements presented in the investigation report, and in particular the movement of the UFOs in the general direction of the wind as well as their appearance, it is very likely that these objects were simply debris from a balloon that burst in flight or, more likely, combustion debris from a nearby fire. We can conclude that this case should be classified as Category B, as a probable observation of light and disparate debris carried by the wind.

summary: Observation of the silent and straight passage of a flying object shaped like a weaver's shuttle: strange unidentified phenomenon.
description: On August 8, 2012, a witness lying on a terrace was gazing at the starry sky when he observed the straight movement of an unrecognizable object for five seconds. This object had the shape of a "weaver's shuttle," brownish-green in color, with blurred edges. A dark red, round shape was seen in the center of the object. The whole thing appeared very blurry but remained identifiable against the background of the sky, which it obscured. No sound was heard during the straight movement from northeast to southwest. This object moved with its major axis oriented perpendicular to the direction of motion. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the objective elements gathered during the investigation (see the investigation report), namely: - The shape and appearance of the UFO. - Its speed and trajectory were inconsistent with a passive object propelled by the wind present on the day and at the time of the observation. - Estimated speed, altitude, and/or size do not conform to those of a motorized, manufactured craft (no unusual noise). We can conclude that the UFO observed by the witness does not resemble any known object or phenomenon. This case is classified as D1, as the observation of an unidentified phenomenon. This testimony is of good consistency: precise and containing numerous details, but observed from a distance, by a single witness, and without a photograph. The observation is strange because it is a UFO with an unusual appearance, difficult to compare to anything known.

summary: Observation of the high-altitude passage of two bright objects flying in parallel: probable passage of satellites.
description: On August 8, 2012, at 11:10 PM, a witness observed two very bright objects passing in parallel at very high altitude for one minute. Their testimony was very brief, and no other accounts were reported. Reading the satellite pass log compiled by Calsky, several satellite passes were observed at that time (11:10 PM): first, the International Space Station (ISS), extremely bright (magnitude -4.3), to which the Russian Progress cargo spacecraft and the Japanese HTV-3 cargo spacecraft were docked. Its apparent trajectory was from southwest to northeast. At approximately the same time, two other, much less bright satellites (IGS5 H2A Rocket and Alos, magnitudes 2.7 and 3 respectively) were observed, following a trajectory from south to north, approximately 80 arcseconds apart. While the witness could hardly have missed the spectacular passage of the ISS, it is surprising that he describes a south-to-north passage, and only one very bright point is visible. If he saw the other two satellites, they were not very bright. Due to this uncertainty and the imprecision of the testimony, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of satellites, without being able to determine precisely which ones.

summary: Observation of the passage of a point of light: passage of the ISS.
description: An amateur astronomer living near the Istres air base, experienced in observing a wide variety of aircraft, witnessed a powerful light at 10:25 PM on August 7, 2012. The light maintained a constant course and an estimated altitude between 1,000 and 2,000 meters. The phenomenon, coming from the southwest, moved to the northeast in approximately 5 minutes and then disappeared. The witness's description and the time of the light's passage are entirely consistent with the observation of a pass of the International Space Station (ISS): see the Calsky report. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation of the displacement OE of a bright luminous sphere: lack of information.
description: witness observed a bright, luminous sphere moving across the sky on August 7, 2012, at approximately 9:31 PM. The account strongly suggests the passage of a large satellite in low Earth orbit (300 to 400 km). However, a check using the global satellite database shows no correlation with this observation. It could be an uncatalogued object (military satellite). In the absence of precise information, GEIPAN classifies this unusual case as "C".

summary: Observation of the silent movement at low altitude of several shapes of varied colors and rapidly flashing: probable LED balloons.
description: On Sunday, August 5, 2012, shortly after 10:00 PM, a young couple returning home from Nice took the D2564 and were surprised to see, while driving and then stopping at the roadside, five or six shapes of varying colors moving silently and flashing rapidly. These shapes moved westward on a downward trajectory and were quickly hidden by a hill. The observation lasted less than a minute. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witnesses' lack of knowledge about the existence of luminescent balloons is undoubtedly the cause of the strangeness and the reason for this statement. After investigation (see the report), the observed phenomenon appears to have been composed of several luminescent balloons whose bright, changing colors are attributed to LEDs located inside. These helium-filled balloons would thus be carried by the easterly wind blowing that evening: the speed and trajectory would be consistent with a maximum distance of approximately 300 meters between the UFO and the witnesses; this would also explain the absence of noise. The presence of two dead-end roads with very little traffic above the observation site could reasonably have been the playing field for this balloon party. Finally, it was a summer evening and a weekend, conducive to festive events of this kind. GEIPAN classifies this case as B (phenomenon probably identified): LED balloons; observation of luminescent balloons for which the person who released them could not be found.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of several luminous orange shapes: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 4, 2012, at approximately 11:00 PM, a witness observed five orange oval shapes moving slowly and silently across the sky. The witness noted that the shapes gathered together before beginning a slow ascent. The witness then lost sight of the shapes as their brightness gradually diminished. This observation perfectly matches the observation of a flying lantern. The release of flying lanterns is very common on Saturday evenings during the summer: numerous local festivals and weddings. As local mountain winds are very complex, especially in the late afternoon during the summer, the wind speed recorded by the nearby weather station (Geneva) does not perfectly match the observed movement. GEIPAN did not conduct a local investigation to identify the perpetrators of this lantern release. The witness is skeptical of this hypothesis, presenting arguments to which GEIPAN has responded (see correspondence). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of thae lanterns.

summary: Brief observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon with a trail: probable observation of a bolide.
description: On August 2, 2012, at 12:08 a.m., two people were intrigued by the rapid and silent passage of a luminous phenomenon across the sky, followed by a trail. This sighting had all the characteristics of a bolide (meteorite fall). The BOAM database recorded numerous bolide sightings that night, but not this one (note that southern France has few meteorological cameras). The webastro forum indicated other simultaneous sightings of the same phenomenon, seemingly identified as such by an amateur astronomer. GEIPAN classified this case as "B": probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.

summary: Observation and photographs of a bright point of multiple colours in the sky: mistaken for the star Arcturus.
description: Recent report (December 5, 2014) of a previous observation. On July 28, 2012, at 11:00 PM, a witness observed a bright point of color (red/yellow/green) from their window, which intrigued them. This point was stationary. In photographs taken after a few seconds of observation, they noted the presence of three points forming a triangle. The object disappeared, then four points reappeared. The observation lasted only a few minutes in the clear sky. No other reports were collected. The witness observed and photographed a point-like luminous phenomenon twice, a few seconds apart. In the direction indicated by the witness, Arcturus, Saturn, and Mars were visible. By carefully examining photograph Ne 2 and comparing it to the environment of the star Arcturus, there is no doubt that it was indeed this celestial body that was photographed (see the investigation report). The appearance and subsequent disappearance of the star is explained by the presence of clouds that evening. The three visible points (instead of a single light for Arcturus) in photograph Ne 1 are explained by the instability of the handheld camera. The variation in colors can be explained by atmospheric turbulence. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of the star Arcturus.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a dark object in the sky in an urban area: probable observation of flying debris carried by the wind.
description: On July 27, 2012, at 8:23 AM, a witness observed a large, dark-colored object moving silently at a constant speed in the sky. The investigation shows that the object's speed and direction of movement are consistent with the wind conditions at the time of the observation. Furthermore, despite the object flying over a densely populated area during rush hour, no other reports were collected. The object observed by the witness is most likely just wind-blown debris. This testimony is fairly consistent: precise, but coming from a single witness and without a photograph. The observation is moderately unusual. The observed object exhibits some dynamic characteristics consistent with those of a passive object carried by the wind; it could be an object with typical behavior. This case is classified as a probable observation of wind-blown debris.

summary: Observation of orange lights passing across the sky forming a triangular shape: lack of information.
description: witness reported an observation made on July 27, 2013, around 3:30 a.m.: the witness twice observed the rapid and silent passage across the sky of orange lights forming a triangular shape. The first passage followed an east-west trajectory (OE), and the second an east-west trajectory (EO). No other accounts were collected. Given the following: - No information on the exact azimuth of appearance and disappearance. - No information on the angular altitudes of appearance and disappearance. - The number of objects in each formation is not specified. - The relative positions of the objects within the formations are not specified. - There are no angular measurements, either for the dimensions of the formations or for individual objects. This account is of rather weak consistency: it lacks important elements for assessment, comes from a single witness, and has no photograph. The observation is moderately unusual: the shapes are not commonplace, but the movement is linear, and the phenomenon is distant. The lack of information prevents us from concluding in favor of a hypothesis. This case should be classified as category C, as it represents an observation of a phenomenon that cannot be identified in its current state; the lack of evidence prevents us from forming a firm opinion.

summary: Observation of the movement in the sky of a first light followed by a second on the same trajectory and at constant speed and distance: rare observation of the passage of the ISS and the Japanese HTV space cargo ship.
description: On July 27, 2012, between 4:20 and 4:25 AM, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of a milky white, oval-shaped light across the sky. The observation lasted approximately 45 seconds before a second, orange light appeared, its trajectory mirroring the first. These lights moved at a constant distance and speed along a straight path. The phenomenon then disappeared, hidden by the surrounding landscape. The witness was fortunate enough to observe a pass of the International Space Station (ISS) (magnitude -3, like Venus) and the Japanese cargo spacecraft HTV (magnitude 3) a few hours before its docking with the ISS (see Calsky record and the Canadian Space Agency website). They were in the same orbit, a few degrees apart. This case is classified as "A" and is clearly identified as an observation of a very rare ISS + HTV pass. It should be noted that the witness described the object as being the size of the Moon, and for an observation lasting 45 seconds: this type of error in assessment is not uncommon for surprising phenomena.

summary: Observation of lights and a grey triangle passing across the sky in a straight SSW-NNE trajectory: lack of information.
description: Around 10 PM on July 26, 2012, two witnesses were intrigued by the observation of three lights (two white and one blue) at the apex of a gray triangle passing overhead. This observation of three bright points crossing the sky in a straight line is somewhat strange, as it could be attributed to the simultaneous passage of three satellites; however, the witnesses clearly stated that they saw a dark triangle between these points, which would make the phenomenon even stranger. GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information and Experimentation on Astronomy) was unable to clearly correlate the observation with known satellites, despite considering two possible satellites. The testimony is somewhat unreliable since the two witnesses were not independent, and there are no photos or videos. The date of the observation remains somewhat uncertain. Given these uncertainties, this case is classified as C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of a vapor ball with a trail along a straight trajectory: unexplained phenomenon.
description: On July 26, 2012, at 10:20 PM, a witness on his balcony was intrigued by the rapid and silent passage of a faint, vaporous sphere across the clear sky. During the object's north-south movement, the witness observed bright spots below it, as well as several small trails of light behind it. The observation lasted six seconds before the object was obscured by the roof of the house. No other witnesses were reported. This is a case of a phenomenon moving in a straight line, and therefore of moderate strangeness, but its highly unusual appearance makes it all the more perplexing. A relatively large number of hypotheses must be considered, as the phenomenon is similar to various causes (see investigation report), but none are entirely satisfactory. The case is well-supported, with a high-quality, very precise, and well-documented witness statement written immediately after the observation. But this remains a single testimony, without photos or videos. GEIPAN, having been unable to confirm any of the hypotheses considered, classifies this case as D1, meaning unexplained.

summary: Observation of a moving, white, luminous point, moving slowly from Southwest to Northeast: passage of the ISS.
description: On July 26, 2012, at 5:10 AM, a witness observed a bright white point of light moving slowly from southwest to northeast, silently. The witness observed the passage of the International Space Station (ISS) (see the sky chart from the Heavens-above website showing the ISS's path. Note: view the chart with east on the left). This is a Class A event: observation of the ISS passing overhead.

summary: Successive observations of different phenomena in the sky: lack of information
description: On July 23, 2012, at 10:45 PM, two witnesses on a beach successively observed phenomena that intrigued them. Three distinct phenomena were briefly reported by the two witnesses. No other testimonies were collected. This case presents a fairly high degree of strangeness, but is rather weak in its evidence: indeed, there are two witnesses, but they are not independent, and it is surprising, at a time when there are still many walkers on the beach, that no other witness came forward. It is also noted that the observation was very brief. The investigation did not reveal any similarities with classic misinterpretations. Due to a lack of corroborating evidence, this case is classified as C.

summary: Observation of three bright points in the sky: astronomical observation of the planets Venus and Jupiter and the star Aldebaran.
description: witness reported an observation made on July 17, 2012, at 4:03 AM: from his terrace, he observed two particularly bright points in the sky in the direction of the East-Southeast. He filmed his observation and, upon reviewing the video, discovered a third point. This arrangement appeared to him as a triangle. He made the same observation two days later. The observation of two very bright, fixed points of light points points to an astronomical origin: the star chart for that day indicated the simultaneous presence of Venus and Jupiter that morning, in the direction of the East/Northeast (see astronomical chart). The witness's video is consistent with the position of these celestial bodies in the sky. The third, less bright point of light is Aldebaran, a very bright star (magnitude -0.6). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as perfectly identified: observation of the planets Venus and Jupiter, and the star Aldebaran.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of an orange light in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On July 14, 2012, at 10:50 PM, during community festivities and before the fireworks display began, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of an orange light from east to west. The object's appearance (an orange halo), its movement in the prevailing westerly wind (see Meteociel report), its short duration, and the fact that it was observed on Bastille Day are all consistent with the passage of a Thai lantern. The witness, unfamiliar with this type of object, was unable to estimate its actual distance or size. GEIPAN did not conduct an investigation to identify the perpetrators of the lecher. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of three luminous objects in the sky: probable observation of luminous balloons or Thai lanterns.
description: On July 14, 2012, around midnight, a motorist was intrigued by the silent movement of three white lights across the sky, which were quickly obscured by the landscape. The witness reported this observation in 2013, along with another observation made seven years earlier. The witness recounted two observations on the same questionnaire. The first, too imprecise, was not considered. For the second observation, the fact that it occurred on the evening of July 14th suggests three festive objects carried by the wind: illuminated balloons or Thai lanterns. The very short duration of the observation makes it impossible to deduce the direction of movement of the objects, or to correlate it with the wind (a strong northwesterly wind: tramontane). The variation in the lights suggests a lantern, but they are generally perceived as yellow or orange. This case does not present all the characteristics of Thai lanterns, but is certainly linked to three luminous objects carried by the wind. GEIPAN classifies case "B": observation of luminous balloons or thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of a bright ball passing through and separating into two: probable atmospheric re-entry of space debris.
description: Three people observed a bright, yellow, brightly colored sphere moving slowly eastward on July 11, 2012, at 9:30 PM. The sphere split in two before disappearing. No sound was heard during the passage. After ruling out the possibility of a Thae lantern (eastward movement inconsistent with the northwest wind, separation into two objects), the hypothesis of atmospheric reentry of space debris was favored: the witness's description, the fragmentation, the duration, and the eastward movement were all consistent. The Calsky catalog of atmospheric reentries lists two entries for that day, but they do not appear to correspond to this event (near-polar orbits). The BOAM (Bureau of Meteor Observers) catalog lists nothing for that time. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of atmospheric reentry of space debris.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a shape that is both triangular and rounded, on which the sun is reflected: probable observation of a festive balloon.
description: On July 9, 2012, between 9:30 and 9:50 PM, a witness was intrigued by the sighting of an object in the sky. A shape described as both rounded and triangular moved silently before disappearing into a cloud. The object's vertical movement (light local wind: see weather report), its reflection, and its shape (see balloon example in the appendix) strongly suggest a helium-filled party balloon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of a party balloon.

summary: Observation of a bright point passing in a straight line and then in a zigzag pattern in the sky: probable observation of a satellite.
description: From his garden, a witness observed a bright point of light in a clear, cloudless sky on July 8, 2012, around 11:30 PM. The point's trajectory, initially straight, continued in a zigzag pattern from north to south for several minutes. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The witness's description of the straight portion of the trajectory strongly suggests a satellite, many of which pass by at that time (see the Calsky list). The zigzag at the end of the trajectory is unusual but may be a consequence of the physiological phenomenon of autokinetic motion (see pages 26 and 27 of the document "Aids to identification of flying objects," currently available on the GEIPAN website via the news section). Several satellites are candidates according to the Calsky website; IGS 1A seems the most likely (see the satellite passage document). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a satellite, observed along part of its trajectory with an autokinetic phenomenon.

summary: witness observed the silent movement of 8 to 10 reddish-orange balls: a probable sighting of Thai lanterns passing by.
description: A witness reported an observation made on Saturday, July 7, 2012, around 10:40 PM. He observed the silent east-west passage of several yellow-orange orbs, all aligned and equidistant from one another. The witness's description immediately suggested the presence of Thai lanterns: a horizontal passage of fireballs, in groups, without noise, from east to west. In Strasbourg, a light wind was blowing from the north at 11:00 PM, but from the south at 8:00 PM; it is difficult to confirm that the wind was blowing from the east in Niedermodern, but it is conceivable. Private parties are numerous on summer Saturday evenings, and many end with the release of Thai lanterns. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Successive observations of yellow luminous phenomena: flight of the partouille of France.
description: On July 6, 2012, starting at 9:50 PM, several people were intrigued by the observation of luminous phenomena in the sky, appearing numerous times (13 times) throughout the evening. One of the witnesses reported their observation to GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group) and the gendarmerie. This observation by several witnesses described a strange-looking phenomenon, difficult to identify without prior notification. On the first Friday of July, the new class of the Patrouille de France (French Air Force aerobatic demonstration team) performed a nighttime demonstration shortly after sunset over the Salon-de-Provence region. The Alpha Jets are equipped with a powerful landing light in the nose of the aircraft, visible from several tens of kilometers away, if and only if the observer is directly in line with the aircraft. During the aerobatic maneuvers, a distant observer saw a series of luminous points appear and disappear. (See the case of VAUCLUSE (84) 02.07.2008 and APT (84) 02.07.2010 http://www.patrouilledefrance.fr/calendrier/2012-07-05-220000/d-fil-et-pr-sentation-salon-de-provence). This case is class "A": observation by the Patrouille de France.

summary: Observation of two white lights followed at a distance by three "fighter" planes: probable confusion with the navigation lights of fighter jets.
description: On July 5, 2012, at 10:22 PM, a witness (T1) and his wife, in their living room, heard the sound of a jet aircraft. T1 went outside. He was surprised to see two white lights in the sky, followed at a distance by three fighter jets flying at low altitude. The UFOs were lost from sight, obscured by the landscape. Other witness accounts were gathered regarding the aircraft's passage (see the investigation report). A witness (T3) gave a statement to the police. Based on the information gathered in the attached investigation report, the only hypothesis considered is confusion with the tail lights of fighter jets, exacerbated by poor viewing conditions and possibly multiple passes by the same aircraft, the first two of which may not yet have activated their landing lights. This testimony is of very high quality (concise, very precise, neutral, and written very quickly after the observation), and of good consistency because, although it comes from a single witness and without a photograph, we were able to rely on a second testimony filed with the Gendarmerie to investigate the hypothesis. The observation is ultimately not very strange because UFOs are, after investigation, easily identifiable. The initial strangeness stemmed primarily from the fact that witness #1 did not observe the first aircraft during their initial approach phase, their landing lights possibly being off and the observation conditions being unfavorable. GEIPAN classifies this case as category B, indicating probable confusion with the navigation lights of fighter jets.

summary: motorist observed a dark-colored, round to oval-shaped object in the sky. Five other moving shapes were also observed: lack of information.
description: On July 4, 2012, at 7:20 a.m., a motorist driving on the A75 near the town of Authezat (63) was intrigued by the presence of a dark-colored, round to oval-shaped object in the sky. It was stationary, moving towards the Sancy mountains. Six minutes later, while driving on the D2013 between Saint-Amand-Tallende and Aydat near Saint-Saturnin, the motorist saw the object again and observed five other shapes moving at low speed and altitude. The witness initially thought they might be fighter jets. Heading towards Chadrat, the motorist lost sight of the various objects. The observation lasted eight minutes. No other witness statements were collected. This testimony is of limited reliability due to its vagueness, the fact that it came from a single witness, and the absence of a photograph. The observation is not particularly unusual, as it could have been a completely ordinary object. The hypotheses considered (see attached report) are that of an aerostat, a tethered balloon, or a free-flight craft (ultralight aircraft, paraglider, etc.). However, given the information gathered during the investigation, namely: - the analysis of three hypotheses poorly suited to the observation - the lack of information (angular measurements) preventing further verification of the estimates of the size, distance, and altitude of the UFO, this case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of two spheres separated by something resembling a rotating helix: lack of information.
description: On July 3, 2012, at approximately 9:15 PM, a motorist observed a puzzling phenomenon: two spheres separated by something resembling a rotating propeller were moving under a cloudy sky. The object was matte gray and lacked lights. From his vehicle, the witness, a former pilot, did not recognize the object. No other witness statements were collected. After a thorough investigation, no satisfactory hypothesis was retained (see the investigation report). In conclusion, although the witness demonstrated high credibility, and the testimony and reconstruction were flawless, this case of observation lacks additional information and witness statements; it remains of average quality. The strangeness of the case is also moderate, as plausible hypotheses could be proposed, but none could be validated or refuted. GEIPAN classifies this case as C due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of six luminous orange orbs: probable sighting of Thai lanterns
description: On July 1, 2012, at approximately 11:00 PM, a witness observed the silent passage of several orange lights moving along a slightly curved trajectory to the east. These lights abruptly changed direction, heading north before quickly disappearing. The witness's description perfectly matches the observation of a Thai lantern display: orange color, smooth and silent movement influenced by the wind (from southwest to northeast, a weak variable wind weakening, see weather report), and disappearance after a few minutes. GEIPAN did not investigate the possible location of the lecher. (Perhaps the Priory Park, at the end of the Be Festival?) This case is classified as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: observation of the silent passage of a series of red-orange balls: Thai lanterns.
description: On June 30, 2012, at 11:25 PM, two witnesses observed three successive red-orange lights from their terrace. All three moved silently in the same direction. The described behavior of the phenomenon, the photographs and video, the time of day, the silence, and the date (a Saturday night) undoubtedly suggest Thai lanterns. The westerly wind present that day (see report) is consistent with the eastward movement of the objects. This case is classified as "A".

summary: unique testimony of an observation of a gigantic white luminous object floating above a field. Rapid and silent tilt and departure towards the clouds: an unidentified phenomenon.
description: On June 29, 2012, at approximately 6:06 a.m. (for precise timing, see the investigation report), a walker, alerted by his dog, was intrigued by the presence of a bright white object, stationary at low altitude above a field bordering a forest. The observation, which lasted less than twenty seconds, nevertheless allowed the witness to state that the object was large, flat underneath and concave on top. As it began to rain, the object rose slightly, tilted, and moved at high speed toward the cloudy sky. No unusual noise or smoke was observed during the observation by the frightened witness. No other reports of this phenomenon have been collected. This case is unusual in that it is extremely similar to and synchronous with a classic natural phenomenon: the observation of the rising sun between two cloud layers. However, several important elements are inconsistent: - Primarily, the direction of observation: a 54° deviation from the sun, this difference cannot be attributed to uncertainty. - The tilt of the phenomenon before its disappearance: this second element could be explained by a perceptual illusion due to the brightness of the phenomenon, or by analogy to media-covered UFO sightings. - The apparent size of the phenomenon: almost 10 times larger than the image of the sun: overestimation of the apparent diameter of the Moon or the Sun at sunrise is very common, but rarely to this extent. GEIPAN investigators went to the site once to verify the location and directions of observation indicated by the witness and ruled out an unintentional error in direction estimation by the witness. A second visit was made to study the possibility of a complex reflection of the sun allowing it to be observed from a different direction. They were unable to identify a satisfactory hypothesis; however, it should also be noted that the weather conditions that morning were very unusual and, of course, unrepeatable: intense heat and heavy rain the previous day, and heavy cloud cover that morning. Its strangeness is moderate, since the phenomenon is similar to a classic natural phenomenon, but with at least one significant anomalous characteristic. GEIPAN classifies this case as D1, meaning unexplained and of moderate consistency.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of nine bright yellow-white spots in the night sky and clear: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Sunday, June 24, 2012, at 12:20 a.m., a witness and their husband observed about ten bright yellow-white points in the clear sky. The witness noted that these points, which initially appeared stationary, then began to move, gained altitude, and moved toward the horizon at high speed. No noise was heard during the five-minute observation. Only one witness statement was recorded, but a photograph was taken. The observation of orange balls or discs in the sky on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The description, as well as the photograph, are consistent with numerous lantern sightings. The Gendarmerie reached the same conclusion. Consequently, GEIPAN classified the case as category B: probable lantern.

summary: Observation of the passage of a point of light in the sky: observation of the passage of the International Space Station.
description: On June 20, 2012, at approximately 10:50 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of a bright point across the sky. He filmed his observation. After analyzing the hypothesis of a plane seen head-on preparing to land at Roissy Airport, and that of a Thai lantern (the wind was against it), GEIPAN ultimately settled on the hypothesis of the ISS: clear weather, and the passage of the International Space Station, very clearly visible in Paris (see Calsky report), rising at 10:46 PM precisely in the direction indicated by the witness, culminating at 10:51 PM, the time indicated by the witness. This case is classified as "A": ISS sighting perfectly identified.

summary: Observation of the passage of about ten orange or red flying balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 17, 2012, at 12:25 a.m., a couple observed the silent passage of a luminous phenomenon consisting of red balls. The witnesses filmed their observation. This case is typical of Thai lanterns: orange or red balls moving erratically according to the local wind (southwest to northeast), released during the night from Saturday to Sunday. The video confirms this hypothesis (the video shows white objects, probably due to the camcorder's white balance being set to automatic). The witness, who observed the lantern release, believed that they only move vertically and did not accept this hypothesis. A newspaper article in the Républicain Lorrain on August 30, 2012, reports that the person who released the lanterns came forward. The case is classified as Class A: observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of several bright orange balls in the clear night sky: probably Thai lanterns.
description: On August 17, 2012, around 1:00 AM, a couple was driving home when the passenger noticed several bright, non-flashing orange orbs in the clear sky. These lights were at low altitude. Only one witness statement was recorded. The observation of orange orbs in the sky on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The fact that they disappeared after a few minutes is also typical of lanterns (the operating time of their burners). The witness was surprised by the sighting (which also happens with lanterns), but he reported the presence of other observers of these phenomena, and these individuals did not provide statements to either GEIPAN or the police. Consequently, GEIPAN classified the case as B: probable Thai lanterns.

summary: A witness observes the slow and silent movement of about ten red lights: a probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: A witness observed from their home the slow, silent, and straight movement of about ten red lights across the sky. The witness's description, the videos, the movement in relation to the southwest wind, and the time of day, all correspond in every respect to the observation of Thai lanterns, probably released at the end of a festival. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent flight in formation of numerous "transparent spheres"; South North trajectory: strange unidentified phenomenon.
description: On June 17, 2012, at 4:00 AM, a witness on their terrace observed the silent passage of several (10-15) transparent spheres flying across the clear sky for 15 seconds. The entire group quickly moved northward toward a cloud formation, into which everything disappeared. Only one witness statement was recorded. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report, namely: - transparent, spherical objects moving silently at an altitude between 1460 m and 2000 m; - the absence of noise, we can conclude that the UFOs observed by the witness possess characteristics, particularly physical ones, that do not resemble any known natural or man-made object. This case is classified as D1, meaning an observation of objects of unknown nature. This testimony is quite consistent: precise, but coming from a single witness and without a photograph. The observation is strange because these are objects with an unusual appearance, although their behavior does not present any extraordinary aspects.

summary: Observation of orange luminous phenomena close to the ground; sudden extinction: probable ground lights due to human activities.
description: On August 17, 2016, GEIPAN received a questionnaire regarding an observation made in 2012. On June 4, 2012, around 3:00 a.m., a witness observed, through the bay window of their living room, an orange, column-shaped luminous phenomenon, which they located in the direction of the Fourches hill in the town of Langres. After fifteen seconds, the phenomenon abruptly disappeared, but the witness then saw two yellow luminous orbs moving around the location of the initial observation. These two luminous orbs also abruptly disappeared. The following day, the witness went to the presumed location of the observation but found no burnt grass or signs of trampling. Only one witness statement was collected. This observation of a ground phenomenon at 3:00 AM on a hill 2 km away is not unusual, given that the witness described it as a possible campfire or flame and mentioned that the nearby chapel may be used by scouts. It could also be a piece of farm equipment surrounded by people with flashlights. The fact that the witness noticed no signs of burnt grass or trampling at the presumed location the following day does not rule out all the previous hypotheses. The same witness made a similar observation in 2016 (ground lights moving around a central glow) on the same hill (a few dozen meters away), an observation also of low strangeness and probably of the same origin. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as category B: ground lights of the vehicle or campfire type and people with flashlights.

summary: Observation of a dark, stationary object flashing irregularly. Low altitude: probably a tethered balloon.
description: On May 30, 2012, starting at 9:00 PM, a witness observed a dark, stationary object at a low altitude from their balcony. The object emitted irregular flashing lights. It remained in the same position until the witness went to bed, at which point they took a video with their mobile phone. Considering the objective evidence gathered, namely: - weather conditions favorable for tethered ballooning: calm to light winds; - lighting compliant with regulations for the use of tethered aircraft; - suitable terrain for tethered aircraft operation at the azimuth where the object was visible, we can conclude that the observed object was very likely a tethered balloon. This testimony is quite consistent thanks to the video, but it lacks essential data (azimuth, size and altitude estimates), which were nevertheless partially reconstructed thanks to the video. The observation is not particularly unusual because it involves an object with ultimately ordinary behavior. This case is classified as B to B as a probable observation of a tethered balloon.

summary: Observation on the ground of flattened grass in a diameter of several meters: lack of information.
description: On May 30, 2012, a witness observed a phenomenon of flattened grass on a plot of woodland belonging to him. The grass, approximately 4 meters in diameter, was flattened and slightly yellowed, and no surrounding traces suggested that an animal or vehicle could have caused it. Given the objective evidence gathered, namely: - A single photograph taken by the witness. - No survey or thorough inspection of the flattened area and its surroundings. The hypothesis of a vortex created by a local wind phenomenon remains the least improbable, but could not be corroborated by relevant weather data or the observation of other local disturbances. We can conclude that, despite the numerous hypotheses developed, none is satisfactory in light of the quantifiable and usable data provided by examining the photograph and the witness statement. This testimony is of rather average quality: fairly precise, but coming from a single witness, with only one photograph and no examination of the scene. The observation is quite strange because it concerns a phenomenon that seems, a priori, unusual. This case is classified as C, meaning the phenomenon cannot be identified at this stage, as the lack of information prevents a firm conclusion.

summary: Observation in the sky of the fall of a luminous phenomenon: certain observation of a bolide.
description: An amateur astronomer was observing the sky towards Mars on Monday, May 28, 2012, at 1:10 AM when he suddenly noticed a white trail followed by a reddish-orange fireball. The phenomenon then disappeared, hidden by the roof of the church to the northwest. A muffled bang was heard. The next day, despite searching the area around his home, no trace of the phenomenon was found on the ground. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report (namely the shape, color, and behavior of the object; the presence of a white trail and characteristic noises; the existence of other eyewitness accounts and video recordings showing the same phenomenon during the same time period; and the disappearance of the phenomenon to the northwest, confirmed by one of the video recordings), we can conclude that the phenomenon exhibits all the characteristics of a bolide (meteoroid fall, commonly called a meteorite), observed from Normandy and the Paris region. This case is classified as Ae as a confirmed observation of a bolide.

summary: Long observation of the silent passage of a luminous object at low altitude in the sky over Dieppe: lack of information.
description: On May 24, 2012, at 11:55 PM, two witnesses in the port area of Dieppe (76) observed a luminous object flying at low altitude in the clear, starry sky. The object was elongated and white. It passed in front of the harbor, then moved over the beach and slowly towards the sea and the open water. The trajectory was straight. The observation lasted a total of 30 minutes without any unusual noise being noticed. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the objective evidence gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - Object flying slowly at very low altitude over the Dieppe urban area. - No wind to light and blowing in the opposite direction to the object's movement. - Some factual elements suggest a possible drone. The possibility of a helicopter was considered, but could not be confirmed. We can conclude that the UFO observed by the witnesses cannot be explained by the available evidence, but it does present characteristics compatible with the plausible hypotheses considered. This testimony is of average consistency: precise but lacking in detail and without a photograph, coming from a single witness. The absence of testimony from witness #2 is regrettable, as is the lack of response to a request for an interview. The observation is strange because it involves an object with characteristics that do not entirely conform to known flying objects, but also do not exhibit extraordinary flight characteristics. Lacking information to support either hypothesis, particularly the absence of a second testimony and the interview with the witness, GEIPAN classifies this case as Category C due to insufficient information.

summary: Observation of a silent flying object stationary then ascending; change of shape and color: case class in to D1 to as observation of an object of unknown nature.
description: On May 21, 2012 (the precise date was confirmed during the investigation), at 10:12 PM, a motorist noticed a luminous phenomenon passing north-south in the overcast sky, which intrigued him. While stopped at a red light, he observed a cylindrical shape "resembling an iceberg with its point facing the ground." Getting out of his vehicle, he found the object stationary and a powerful light emanating from small portholes. A luminous orange sphere was also observed around the object. The object then began an upward trajectory, changed shape (inverted V) and color (white), and disappeared into the cloud cover. The observation lasted a total of 15 seconds. Only one witness statement was collected. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report, namely: - Unusually shaped object with portholes and lights. - Stationary above the road in front of the witness. - It departed after a few seconds, changing shape. We can conclude that the UFO observed by the witnesses is inexplicable and presents numerous characteristics that are difficult to reconcile with the only plausible hypothesis considered: that of a party balloon. This case should be classified as D1, as an observation of an object of unknown nature. This testimony is quite consistent: very precise, but coming from a single witness and without a photograph. It is surprising that, in the middle of the city, no one else noticed the phenomenon. The observation is strange because it concerns an object whose physical and dynamic characteristics are unusual and do not strictly conform to any known flying object.

summary: Observations of the passage of more than one hundred lights associated with frightening shapes in the sky: licking of Thai lanterns on the occasion of a wedding.
description: On May 19, 2012, at 11:20 PM, several members of the same family observed hundreds of lights in the sky, associated with shapes that frightened them. No sound was heard during the passage of the UFOs over their property. The Gendarmerie conducted a local investigation and identified the event as the release of 100 Chinese lanterns during a wedding, a few hundred meters from the witnesses. GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) verified the compatibility of the phenomenon with the local wind. GEIPAN confirmed the Gendarmerie's investigation findings and classified this case as "A," clearly identified as the release of Thai lanterns. The witnesses' interpretation of this large-scale phenomenon was heavily influenced by surprise and fear.

summary: Intermittent observation of a luminous object in the sky: probable observation of the sun's reflections on a glider in flight.
description: On May 18, 2012, between 5:30 and 6:00 PM, two people were intrigued by a phenomenon in the clear sky. One of the witnesses filmed the movement of an object that occasionally lit up in the sky. The video footage is of poor quality and therefore unsuitable for measuring the object's size, distance, and speed. Given the objective evidence gathered—namely, the presence of a glider airfield nearby, gliders painted white to enhance the reflection of sunlight, the object's movement consistent with that of a glider thermalling, and weather conditions favorable for gliding—we can conclude that the object observed by the witnesses was probably a glider from Avignon-Pujaut airfield, performing thermalling spirals, and whose wings and/or fuselage intermittently reflected sunlight. This case is classified as a B-type observation of a glider performing aerobatics near Avignon-Pujaut airfield, its components intermittently reflecting sunlight.

summary: Multiple observations of the silent, zigzag movement of luminous balls in the sky: observation of reflections of the sun on satellites.
description: The witness reports multiple observations in the sky since 2011. The most recent phenomena occurred on Saturday, May 12, 2012, around 11:05 PM, on Tuesday, May 15, 2012, around 11:53 PM, and on Tuesday, June 5, 2012, at 12:19 AM. Each time, the objects were luminous spheres, bright like stars, moving across the sky in a zigzag pattern, capable of accelerating, descending, and ascending very rapidly and silently. The observations mentioned correspond precisely to flashes of light on the Iridium and Metop satellites (see the Calsky records). Other observations likely correspond to other satellites: the impression of slight zigzags along the trajectories of luminous points observed against a black background is common; it is an illusion, called autokinetic, due to the micromovements the eye makes to track the point in the sky. The impression of distance and approach arises from variations in the brightness of objects: an object whose brightness decreases is interpreted as moving away. This type of observation is classified as "A": observation of sunlight reflecting off satellites.

summary: Observation of the rapid and rectilinear movement of a luminous point projecting a bright light: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry.
description: The witness observed a large, bright, disc-shaped point of light emitting a very vivid white light. Its rapid movement followed a straight, NW-SE trajectory at a constant altitude. This very bright disc, crossing the sky in 8 to 10 seconds, strongly suggests the atmospheric reentry of a satellite debris or, more likely, a meteoroid (meteorite). This phenomenon, called a bolide, is very spectacular. The BOAM network did not record this specific event, but reported numerous similar events on the same night; this is the period of several meteor showers, particularly the Eta Aquarids, which is the most intense of this time of year. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a bolide, caused by the atmospheric reentry of a natural object.

summary: Observation of the passage of three orange lights: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 6, 2012, at 10:11 PM, a witness was intrigued by what he saw in the sky: three orange lights moving across the sky along a north-south trajectory. Two of the lights disappeared abruptly, while the third fell towards the ground and was lost from sight behind buildings. The appearance of the lights (orange orbs), the duration of a few minutes, and their slow, silent movement strongly suggest Thai lanterns. Two hours after the presidential election results, some may have wanted to celebrate the event by releasing lanterns. The weak and unstable wind could explain the delay between the arrival of the lights in the sky (this is reinforced by perspective); the brightness of the flame meant that even at a short distance (100m) the details of the object could no longer be distinguished. Furthermore, it appears that for one of the lanterns, part of the burning paraffin block broke off and fell to the ground. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observations of the movement of orange luminous phenomena: probable passage of Thai lanterns.
description: Witnesses reported observing several orange lights silently moving between 11:00 PM and 11:30 PM on May 6, 2012. The phenomenon appeared to fade and disappear after several minutes of observation. The appearance of the lights (orange orbs), their movement with the easterly wind, the duration of a few minutes, and their slow, silent motion strongly suggest Thae lanterns, likely launched by a voter pleased with the outcome of the presidential election. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of red balls in the sky: probably Thai lanterns.
description: On May 5, 2012, around 10:00 PM on Hattes Beach near Mana in French Guiana, a witness observed intriguing luminous phenomena. Several red spheres moved slowly and silently across the sky. Considering the objective evidence gathered (the red color of the observed and photographed objects, their slow and simultaneous movement along an upward trajectory, no or very light winds, and the fact that it was a day of the week suitable for launching lanterns, as well as the recent establishment of a lantern vendor in the department), we can conclude that the three objects observed and photographed by witness ne1 were most likely sky lanterns, also known as Thai lanterns. This case is classified as B, indicating a very probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Successive observations of the passage of two groups of orange light points in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 30, 2012, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness observed a bright orange point in the sky, followed by three other points. These moved along a continuous upward trajectory before gradually disappearing into the sky. The witness recorded videos. While the videos show a low degree of strangeness and good consistency, despite some inaccuracies in the directions that are quite common, this observation has all the characteristics of a misinterpretation due to a group of Thai lanterns being licked during festivities on the eve of May Day. Since the local wind direction could not be definitively determined, despite a generally consistent trend before the storm around the observation site, verifying the correlation between the local wind and the movement of the objects was insufficient. It was also noted that rain was not conducive to lantern licking. GEIPAN did not investigate the perpetrators of the lantern licking. In light of this observation, GEIPAN classifies this case as B, as a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a grey object passing across the sky: probable balloon.
description: On Sunday, April 29, 2012, at approximately 4:15 PM, a witness observed a gray, spherical shape passing below the clouds. Intrigued, the witness filmed the object, which moved along a straight trajectory. A plume of white smoke or flames was seen by the witness beneath the object. It then disappeared, hidden by a neighboring building. The object's almost linear movement, consistent with the wind direction (south to southwest), which was strong that day, strongly suggests a balloon. Because it was seen against the light, it appeared dark. It was not spherical; therefore, as it rotated, it sometimes reflected sunlight, causing temporary flashes. The object's relative clarity suggested it was relatively close (less than 1 km) and therefore of modest size (less than 1 meter). The small, swirling white dots could be pollen, common at this time of year during these first mild spring days, and very bright when viewed against the light. No other reports of this phenomenon have been collected. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a festive balloon, likely originating from Ars-sur-Moselle or even further south.

summary: Observation of a yellow luminous phenomenon with movements: observation of the Moon with optical illusion for its movement.
description: witness reported an observation made on April 27, 2012, at 12:20 a.m. above the ponds of Grec and Perols in Carnon Plage. The yellow luminous phenomenon was in the shape of a crescent moon, almost stationary before moving back and forth. No noise was heard during the 40-minute observation. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. The direction of the phenomenon indicated by the witness (see witness's sketch) is very close to the Moon's position in the sky (azimuth of 290°, see astronomical chart of the western sky). The video shows that the observed object is indeed the Moon, occasionally obscured by clouds. The apparent westward movements of the object are an optical illusion due to the eastward movement of the cloud base (see weather report). This case is classified as "A": observation of the Moon with an optical illusion of movement.

summary: Observation of the movement of a very bright phenomenon: lack of information.
description: On April 19, 2012, at approximately 10:40 PM, a witness observed a very bright point in the sky, heading north-northwest. This point, initially stationary, then appeared to move. The direction indicated by the observer (west-northwest) corresponds to the position of the planet Venus in the sky, at an elevation of 15 arcseconds above the horizon. The object's movements, as reported by the observer, are clearly inconsistent with this hypothesis. The possibility of an aircraft was considered, but radar data could not be obtained in time. Given this insufficient information, GEIPAN classified this unusual case as "C" due to a lack of details.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of two bright orange-fire phenomena which went out simultaneously: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 15, 2012, around midnight, a witness observed the silent movement of a round, orange sphere that appeared to be on fire. The object moved along a downward trajectory to the east, then turned south. A second, seemingly identical phenomenon (also on fire and orange) was seen and appeared to be joined by the first: the two UFOs moved together along the same course. The brightness of both UFOs gradually decreased, and then they went out at the same time. Only one questionnaire was collected. Based on the descriptions, it can be concluded that these were two objects carried by the wind, as they followed the same trajectory; indeed, the witness also reached this conclusion. ("The appearance and behavior of the phenomenon made me think it was very light and carried by the wind.") The wind measured at ground level at the airport is from the N-NW (15 km/h), which does not preclude, at higher altitudes (influenced by the city, hills, or forests), meandering wind patterns that could explain a direction of movement from the West and then from the North. The two UFOs follow each other on the same trajectory with a slight offset. The perception of one UFO converging with the other is subjective, as it occurs when the UFOs are seen from the same direction, and therefore with distances that are difficult to judge. The orange color and the final extinction (in flight) of the two UFOs are characteristic of Thai lanterns, and a weekend night is conducive to such festive events. The description of flames at the rear of the UFO is strange for Thai lanterns, which can indeed ignite but then fall quite quickly. However, the perception of flames is often subjective; it can be induced by the flickering of a lantern's light for those unfamiliar with the full range of lantern illumination, or even more so in this case by atmospheric turbulence and conditions of drizzle or light rain. This does not detract from the accuracy of the witness's account, who is an airline pilot. The investigation benefits from a careful reconstruction of the trajectory, which the witness faithfully established based on their angular perception (since a witness has only this information). On their drawing, they place the appearance of the second UFO five to six times farther away than the closest approach of the first, and therefore from an angular perception that is a priori five or six times smaller. However, the same perception of fire occurred with this UFO, which was 5 or 6 times smaller and no larger than 1/10 of a moon (according to the angular measurements provided by the witness), reinforcing the subjective nature of the "flames" appearance. The "flames behind" appearance is the only unusual element in an otherwise unfamiliar picture, where everything points to wind-borne objects, particularly Thai lanterns. But it is entirely possible that this appearance resulted from a difficulty in perception (or misinterpretation) exacerbated by less than optimal atmospheric conditions. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes that the observation likely involved Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the West-East passage of an object in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On April 15, 2012, at 10:31 PM, a witness observed an object in the clear sky, initially stationary and then moving from west to east at low altitude. A muffled sound was heard. The object passed over the building, and the witness lost sight of it. The brief observation, however, allowed the witness time to record a video with their cell phone. No other witness accounts were reported. It appears this sighting was likely the result of mistaking a passenger plane for one approaching Roissy Airport. The most unusual aspect of this observation is the witness's confusion: residing along the flight path of Roissy, the witness must be familiar with the heavy air traffic to this international airport, even though only a portion of this traffic actually flies over their home, which is 50 km from the runway threshold. The photo and video footage could have helped to further investigate the case; the witness did not provide it directly but shared it via online services. This footage is no longer accessible and could not be used. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C due to a lack of information, bordering on a B case (Aircraft).

summary: Observation of the passage of a bright white object in the sky: observation of the passage of the International Space Station.
description: On April 13, 2012, at approximately 9:34 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of a luminous object across the sky that he did not recognize. Despite an initial misidentification (later corrected), this observation, of slight strangeness and good consistency, corresponds definitively to the passage of the International Space Station (ISS). There is no doubt that the witness observed the ISS on the evening of April 13 between 9:34 PM and 9:37 PM. The curved trajectory described by the witness stems from an erroneous perception of the orbit, which is actually almost circular; only satellites passing at the zenith create the perception of a linear trajectory. GEIPAN classifies this case as a confirmed observation of the International Space Station.

summary: Observation of the movement of a white light: passage of the ISS.
description: A witness reported an observation made on April 12, 2012, around 10:30 PM. From his balcony, he observed the north-south movement of a white light source for two minutes. No trail or unusual noise was heard during the observation. No other witness statements were collected by the gendarmerie. No known flights were reported to air traffic control in the Dinard airspace at the time of the event. The witness's description perfectly matches the observation of the International Space Station (ISS) passing over Brittany that evening: see the ISS's tracking path against the sky (the time indicated on the path is only accurate to within a few minutes). This case is classified as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS).
