summary: Observation of a fixed red glow in the sky; change of color and sudden disappearance: lack of information.
description: On April 12, 2012, at approximately 9:40 PM, a witness's attention was drawn to a rather bright red glow that suddenly appeared behind the glass of their first-floor window. The observation lasted several minutes before the light changed color and intensity, diminishing and disappearing. No other witness statements were collected. Rated to be of low to moderate strangeness and of similar consistency, this case of observation remains difficult to interpret: an apparently fixed point of light, bright orange-red in color and turning white as it faded, suggests an aircraft seen head-on, but not definitively in the absence of air traffic records (see the investigation report). GEIPAN classifies this case as Category C in the absence of other objective evidence.

summary: Observation of a twinkling star: astronomical observation of Venus.
description: witness reported observing the sky on April 8, 2012, first around 10:00 PM and then again around 11:30 PM. The witness filmed their last observation. The direction indicated by the witness (the Jura Mountains) at an azimuth of approximately 290° coincides perfectly with the position of the planet Venus, which the witness did not mention. The planet Venus, particularly visible at this time of year, surprises many witnesses when it is low on the horizon: it is then interpreted as an object flying past the Earth. The same celestial body, observed by the witness an hour and a half earlier, was then high in the sky; it was not interpreted by the witness as a strange object. Regarding the video: a point of light against a black background filmed by a video camera with the zoom fully extended produces numerous optical and electronic artifacts. The diamond shape is a result of the camera's aperture, which appears when the focus is incorrect (at night, many cameras in autofocus mode struggle to focus, alternating between blurry and sharp images). The colors are due more to noise, electronic interference, and optical aberrations (even with a very high-quality camera) than to the actual image of the filmed object. Therefore, the video doesn't provide much information about the observed object. This case is classified as "A": observation of the planet Venus.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of about a hundred pink luminous points in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 7, 2012, at approximately 11:30 PM, two people observed the silent movement of about a hundred pink lights in the cloudy sky. Two successive groups, as well as other lights following one another in a line, were seen at low altitude. All the lights arrived from the north-northeast and turned due east. The observation lasted 30 minutes. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of a series of white and pink orbs on a weekend night strongly suggests a lantern release, likely from a private party. The ordered movement, including changes in trajectory, is common with lanterns, as it results from the shared following of the same wind current, which is not necessarily uniform near the ground. White and pink lanterns are very popular for wedding celebrations. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the evolution of two points of light in the sky. The second point evolves around the first, which has a rectilinear trajectory: this case of observation is classified as D1 as unexplained.
description: On Wednesday, April 4, 2012, at 8:15 PM, a witness was intrigued by the movements of two bright yellow or white points of light in the sky, moving from east to north at high speed. The first point followed a straight and uniform trajectory, but it was the second that captivated the witness's attention, as it constantly moved around the first, describing ellipses, making abrupt, acute-angle turns, making contact, and then rapidly returning to its position behind it. The observation ended after about fifteen seconds, when the two points of light disappeared through or behind a cloud. After a field investigation that helped to determine the azimuths, and a cognitive interview that did not provide any significant new information, this case of observation remains highly unusual, given the movements of the second UFO around the first. This case observation resists the usual hypotheses of misinterpretation. Due to the unique nature and brevity of the testimony, the hypothesis of a temporary visual illusion (ophthalmic migraine, phosphenes) remains, but the witness appears to have perfect vision and health and has not reported experiencing similar effects: lacking evidence to support this hypothesis, it has been rejected. The consistency of the case is assessed at 0.7 because the witness is unique and unqualified. The strangeness of the case is assessed at 0.6 due to the non-linear, but distant, movement of the object. Consequently, this case observation is classified as D1, meaning unexplained.

summary: Successive observations over several evenings of the movement of a point of light: astronomical observation of Venus.
description: A person reported several sightings of a bright point in the sky in April 2012. On April 2nd, the witness observed it first with the naked eye and then with binoculars. The witness stated that, for several consecutive nights, they observed a very bright object that slowly descended towards the horizon and disappeared around 12:30 AM. This speed of movement undoubtedly suggests a celestial body, setting like the sun. At that time, Venus, particularly bright (magnitude -5.2), was also noted in the evening sky. The object's appearance as described by the witness is probably the result of an over-interpretation due to visual or optical defects highlighted by the nighttime observation of a very bright point. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," indicating an observation of the planet Venus, which was particularly bright on those nights.

summary: Observations of the silent north-south passage of several non-flashing orange lights: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On March 31, 2012, at approximately 9:15 PM, a witness observed several non-flashing orange lights passing silently in the north-southwest sky. A second witness also observed part of the phenomenon (but did not provide a statement). The observation ended with the lights gradually fading. This sighting has all the characteristics of a Thai lantern display: the movement is consistent with the relatively strong northeasterly wind (17 to 39 km/h), the orange color, the duration of the observation, and the number of objects. Saturday is a night of festivities, and consequently, a time when lantern releases are frequent. GEIPAN did not conduct any investigation to determine who released these sky lanterns. This case is classified as "B": probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Multiple observations at different locations of bright colored points appearing stationary then moving: probable observation of Sirius, followed by Procyon and/or Betelgeuse.
description: On March 26, 2012, around midnight, a witness in Ploeren (56) observed a luminous object moving in the sky towards the south from their terrace. Intrigued, they called the gendarmerie, and a patrol was dispatched to the location, confirming the witness's observation. The patrol then moved to Baden and observed the phenomenon again. Another gendarmerie unit, operating from the Etel bar semaphore station, confirmed the presence of a twinkling point of light in the southwest at an elevation of 20° between 12:45 a.m. and 1:05 a.m. A final observation was made from the GERBAM observatory in Gevres. The object disappeared as it rose at 1:50 a.m. This observation is complex because it comes from several witnesses located in different places; it is also not precise enough regarding the azimuth and elevation of the phenomenon at each stage of observation. The descriptive accounts of the observed object have all the characteristics of very bright stars seen near the horizon (change of color, apparent lateral and fore-and-aft movements). However, it is difficult to definitively identify the celestial body observed, and it is possible that two or three stars were seen successively: Sirius, Procyon, and Betelgeuse, due to temporary obscuration by the cloud cover that followed the afternoon rain. It should also be noted that none of the witnesses mention Sirius or any other star, which would have allowed the phenomenon to be located relative to these celestial bodies, thus ruling out this hypothesis. In any case, given the absence of any phenomenon observed by the patrol aircraft and on radar, it can be stated that the phenomenon was very distant. With all these elements in mind, GEIPAN concludes that the observation was likely of Sirius, followed by Procyon and/or Betelgeuse.

summary: Observation of the silent and rapid movement of a group of 4 lights: probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On March 24, 2012, at approximately 8:20 PM, a witness observed a group of four white lights moving silently and very rapidly in the sky. The witness, an amateur astronomer, reported that the lights appeared near Capella and disappeared when they reached the constellation Ursa Major (the Great Bear). No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. It is highly probable that this is the same phenomenon observed in Valras and Brantôme: the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid, with fragmentation, or of uncatalogued space debris (see the investigation report and the verification performed on SpaceTrack). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid or space debris.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of two red balls in the Parisian sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On March 23, 2012, at 11:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent movement of two red lights above Parisian buildings. They disappeared, hidden by the urban landscape. This sighting has all the characteristics of Thai lanterns: the movement of red lights, silent and uniform, following the wind (from northwest to north, at 6 to 15 km/h), for a few minutes, during a weekend evening or festival. Lechers in the city are indeed not recommended, but they actually occur quite often! GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a formation of five bright points of medium intensity: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of meteoroids.
description: A witness observed five bright points of light moving in formation along a descending trajectory on March 13, 2012, at 8:35 PM. No noise was heard during the observation. Another almost simultaneous report of a very similar appearance was sent to GEIPAN, seen from Saint-Mathieu-de-Tréviers (34) on the same evening, and viewed from the west by this witness. It is highly probable that this was the same phenomenon. The hypothesis of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (meteorite) or space debris is therefore highly likely. Based on this information, GEIPAN classifies this observation as category B, probable observation of atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (meteorite).

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a triangular formation made up of several green-orange lights: probable atmospheric reentry of meteors.
description: On March 13, 2012, at approximately 8:30 PM, a witness observed, from their terrace, the silent passage of a triangular formation composed of several green-orange lights moving at high speed and low altitude. Another witness reported a very similar phenomenon that also occurred that evening. Following an investigation entrusted to an IPN (National Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology) and based on the information received, GEIPAN (French Interministerial Group for Experimental and Paranormal Research) classified this observation as category B, indicating a probable atmospheric reentry of meteoroids (see investigation report).

summary: Short successive observations in the same evening of the passage of red-burgundy objects in the clear sky: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On March 12, 2012, at 8:00 PM, a witness went out onto his terrace and looked at the sky when he spotted three burgundy-red objects in the shape of a cross. These objects crossed the sky from west to north. The sighting lasted only a few seconds. At 10:50 PM, the witness went out onto his terrace again with his partner, and they both saw five objects in the sky moving from north to east. They were quickly obscured by the surrounding landscape (trees and houses in the housing development). Only one witness statement was recorded. The sighting of red flying objects moving in a group across the sky is reminiscent of Thai lanterns licked during a festival. The Météociel weather report for Strasbourg, 40 km away, indicates a light, variable wind from the NE, N, and NW. In this case, the described northeastward movement doesn't correspond well to the local wind; however, this wind was light and variable, and we don't have any very recent weather reports. We cannot formally rule out this hypothesis. Monday is rarely a holiday, which also doesn't support this hypothesis, nor does the cross shape described by the witness. Air traffic data doesn't mention any aircraft that could correspond to the observation. GEIPAN received no other reports of phenomena in the region that day. Due to a lack of precise weather information and a lack of cross-checking, GEIPAN classifies this case in category C.

summary: Observation of the passage of an aircraft followed by three objects forming a triangle: military aerial maneuvers.
description: On March 7, 2012, at approximately noon, a witness was intrigued by the sighting of a passenger plane followed by three objects forming a triangle. The objects were very close to the tail of the aircraft and exchanged positions behind it. The observer witnessed an exceptional maneuver by military aircraft. A detailed explanation is provided in the attached document (radar trace). This case is classified as "A": observation of military aerial maneuvers.

summary: Observations of the passage of four white lights forming the four corners of a rectangle: probable observations of light reflections from car headlights on railway catenaries.
description: On March 4, 2012, at around 8 p.m., a driver and her passenger made an intriguing observation. Stopped at a stop sign, they saw four white lights pass from right to left, forming the four corners of a rectangle several meters above the ground. These lights disappeared at treetop level. No unusual noise was heard. GEIPAN initially considered the possibility of a luminous object carried by the wind, but the wind direction (West) did not correspond to the object's movement (South to North). An investigation with military air traffic control, to search for any aircraft, yielded only negative results. A GEIPAN investigator went to the site at night and observed, then recorded on video, a luminous phenomenon that could perfectly explain the observation: the headlights of cars approaching from the opposite direction were reflected off the overhead power lines of the railway. The reflections move from right to left, then disappear, as the witnesses indicated. It is highly likely that this is the same phenomenon observed by the witnesses. The witness declined to meet with the investigator to further the investigation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of reflections from car headlights on the railway overhead lines.

summary: Probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid or space debris.
description: On Thursday, March 1, 2012, at 10:25 PM, a motorist noticed a striking light in the sky. He observed the passage of a huge yellow "shooting star" with a blue-white border, followed by a blue trail. The size impressed the witness. The appearance of the phenomenon (straight trajectory, very rapid movement, bright light) clearly characterized it as a bolide: the atmospheric reentry of a meteor or space debris. Since the witness indicated a duration of approximately one second, and no reentry of space debris was recorded that day, the hypothesis of a meteorite impact was favored. The REFORME network of meteor observers did not (yet?) report this phenomenon. GEIPAN classified this case as "B".

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a spherical and luminous object: passage of the ISS.
description: On March 1, 2012, at approximately 7:05 PM, a witness observed a luminous, spherical object passing across the sky. Its movement was rectilinear at a constant speed, without any change of direction. The described observation corresponds exactly to the passage of a large satellite. The International Space Station (ISS) was passing over France that evening from northwest to southeast, between 7:00 PM and 7:03 PM. Despite a two-minute discrepancy between the witness's report and the recorded observation of the passage (likely due to the inaccuracy of the witness's watch or the orbit model used for the recording), GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Successive nighttime observations of the slow movement of a point of light: astronomical observations of Venus.
description: Two witnesses reported their extended observations of a very bright phenomenon in the sky. On February 20th and 21st, 2012, at approximately 8:20 PM, a witness in Aveyron observed the slow movement of a particularly bright point of light in the west. The witness used a camera and video camera to view and film the phenomenon. Another witness, located in Tarn, observed "a kind of very, very bright star." The bright point observed by the witnesses corresponds to the planet Venus (see star chart), particularly visible at this time of year and very bright in the sunset. This event is classified as "A".

summary: Probable observation of the passage of a balloon.
description: witness reports an observation lasting a few seconds, made on February 19, 2012, at 9:15 AM. Upon opening a skylight, the witness observed a gray, aluminum-colored, spherical object in the sky passing over their house. It moved silently in a southwest direction, leaving no trail. It disappeared into the clouds. The observed object, moving with the wind, was certainly a balloon filled with helium or hydrogen. It could have been a weather balloon, perhaps launched from Mérignac an hour earlier and arriving in Ares due to wind shifts that had significantly changed during the preceding hour (see weather reports for Bordeaux and Biscarrosse), or more likely, a fairground balloon launched from Lège-Cap-Ferret, or even a pilot balloon launched to prepare for hot air balloon flights. This case is classified as "B," a probable balloon sighting.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a white light in the fog: probable observation of a light animation of the Sky Tracer type.
description: On Saturday, February 18, 2012, around 8:00 PM, a witness observed a curious luminous phenomenon in the sky: an oblong white glow appeared stationary above the farm buildings. It suddenly disappeared but reappeared a few seconds later in the same spot, tracing a geometric figure (half a Z) at high speed before vanishing again. No other reports were collected. Due to its limited strangeness and lack of precise orientation, this observation appears to be a case of mistaken identity involving the movement of a light beam from a SkyTracer-type projector. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a luminous animation.

summary: Observation of a very bright stationary object in the sky; sudden disappearance: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On February 17, 2012, at approximately 8:20 a.m., a driver and her daughter were intrigued by the presence of a bright, silvery-white object in the sky. The light intensity was so great that it was difficult for the witness to precisely describe the object's shape (rather rectangular and quite flat) and its considerable size. The observation of the stationary and silent UFO lasted about twenty seconds. In order to maneuver the vehicle, the witness took their eyes off it for three seconds. The witness did not see the object again in the sky. No other reports of the phenomenon were received by GEIPAN. GEIPAN assigned an investigator to the case: dozens of people were interviewed, but none confirmed the events. And yet, that morning at 8:30 a.m., there were many people taking children to school. The cognitive interview yielded nothing more than the witness's initial report. This brief, uncorroborated sighting while driving is deemed insufficiently substantiated. Given that the witness was driving facing the sun, the sighting could have resulted from the reflection of a bright object in the car's windshield or the sun's reflection on a helicopter in flight, but this hypothesis could not be confirmed. Lacking further testimonies or additional evidence, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to insufficient information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement from East to West of a green light in the sky of the Antilles: probable atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: An air traffic controller at the control tower of Martinique Aimé Césaire International Airport reported an observation made by several people on February 11, 2012, at approximately 11:10 PM. A luminous green phenomenon rapidly crossed the Caribbean sky from east to west. Controllers in Guadeloupe, gendarmes on the ground, and the pilots of AFR 3570 (Paris-Martinique) also witnessed it. The phenomenon of a very bright green ball crossing the sky in a few seconds immediately suggests a fireball, the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (meteorite), or space debris. Space debris enters the atmosphere at approximately 7 km/s and crosses the sky over a period of 20 seconds to a few minutes. Given the observed nature and duration of the phenomenon, the hypothesis of atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (meteorite) was retained for this case, class B e

summary: Probable observations of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On February 4, 2012, at approximately 11:15 PM, people in the Yvelines and Aube departments observed a silent, luminous blue-green and orange object moving in the sky. Its trajectory was straight. The eyewitness accounts closely matched the characteristics of an atmospheric reentry. Its west-southwest direction and duration of only a few seconds ruled out the possibility of a space debris reentry. GEIPAN classified this case as "B": probable atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (meteorite fall).

summary: Observation at dusk of a yellowish luminous phenomenon, oblong in shape, slowly following a straight trajectory in the sky: probable airplane contrail.
description: Recent report (January 14, 2015) of a previous observation. On February 3, 2012, at 6:04 PM, a witness observed a luminous, oblong-shaped object in the sky, moving slowly and silently along a straight path. The object disappeared after a few minutes. The observation lasted two minutes, during which the witness took the time to take photographs. No other reports were collected. The witness observed a very bright, yellow, oblong shape moving slowly in a straight line to the North/Northwest. The sun had set approximately 30 minutes earlier. This phenomenon corresponds very well to a condensation trail from a distant aircraft (> 50 km) illuminated by the setting sun. Clear skies are sufficient to observe this type of phenomenon within half an hour of sunset (or before sunrise). See an explanation of "strange aircraft trails" on page 3 of the news section on the website www.cnes-geipan.fr. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of an aircraft contrail.

summary: Observations of the movement of a dark mass in the sky preceded by a loud muffled noise: probable observation of the flight of an unlit aircraft.
description: On February 2, 2012, at 12:45 a.m., several people were intrigued by a loud, muffled noise that seemed to come from a dark, unlit mass moving slowly and at low altitude in the sky. The main witness account corresponded to the observation of a relatively typical, but unlit, motorized flying object, possibly an unauthorized flight (airship, ultralight, or possibly a helicopter) or a military exercise. (See investigation report.) This case is classified as "B": probable sighting of an unlit aircraft.

summary: Multiple observations of the rapid passage of a luminous and multicolored phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of the atmospheric reentry of a natural meteoroid.
description: On January 31, 2012, around 10 p.m., several witnesses observed the rapid passage of a bright, colored phenomenon across the sky. Witnesses in Calmont (31) and Castelnaudary (11) provided more detailed reports of their observations. The testimony of the Calmont witness is the subject of a specific investigation. This phenomenon does not correspond to any recorded space object (debris) that could have re-entered the atmosphere. The REFORME network (meteor observers) has recorded this meteor, which is very likely a natural meteoroid: indeed, the observation duration, less than 10 seconds, suggests a speed well above 7 km/s, which is the re-entry speed of debris from launch vehicles or satellites. This case is classified as B: probable atmospheric re-entry of a natural meteoroid.

summary: Observation of the zigzag movement of a spherical luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation from the International Space Station (ISS).
description: At 7:35 a.m. on January 30, 2012, a witness observed what he initially thought was a star. The object was spherical, about the size of a 5-cent coin, white, and bluish in the center. Suddenly, the object moved and appeared directly overhead, then zigzagged from right to left, moved off very quickly, zigzagged again, and headed south until it disappeared. It was observed that at precisely the same moment, in directions very close to those indicated by the witness, the International Space Station (ISS) was crossing the sky from northwest to southeast and was extremely bright (magnitude -4, like Venus). The description of the object matches the ISS, but the account of its movement obviously does not, since the ISS moves in a straight line. Since the witness could not have missed the ISS sighting, we conclude that the witness was a victim of classic perceptual illusions: autokinesis and autostasis (the perception of a point of light in the sky), frequent illusions when observing against a uniform background; and because the cloud cover obscured the fainter stars, the ISS was the only point of light visible against the sky. Due to the partially overcast sky, a slight doubt remains regarding the ISS's visibility. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of the International Space Station. The witness made a second sighting on January 22nd, but did not provide details. On that day, a passage of the ISS was observed from 7:06 AM to 7:13 AM above the northern horizon. The witness made a third observation on Friday, February 24th, at 9:20 PM, of "two spheres resembling my last testimony, but bright red in color, which followed each other perfectly." At that precise moment, two American NOSS spy satellites were observed passing close to the northern horizon; however, these satellites are usually too dim to be seen with the naked eye.

summary: Observation of the movement of a silent, silvery, shiny cylindrical object: lack of information.
description: On January 21, 2012, a driver and his passenger were traveling on the A13 motorway towards Caen. Between 4:30 and 5:15 PM, they observed a silent, silvery, shiny cylindrical object in the sky. Initially stationary, it then moved very rapidly along an east-west trajectory. The object disappeared, leaving a plume of cloud. Only one witness statement was received by GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena). Several hypotheses were considered for this sighting: an aircraft or a cylindrical thermal balloon (gray or transparent) that may have temporarily reflected sunlight. To verify one of these hypotheses, GEIPAN requested radar data from the French Air Force. Only one radar track, of unusable quality, was found in the area and did not correspond to the witness statement. On the other hand, the witness indicated in the questionnaire that the object "came from the East moving towards the West," then in subsequent email exchanges on March 22, 2012, he stated that the object came from the Northwest. The time of the phenomenon is only known to within about half an hour, which is too long to correlate with aircraft flyovers. The location of the observation during a highway trip is also imprecise. The observed aircraft do not appear on radar, and the only radar trace produced proves unusable; there is no solid evidence to confirm or refute any hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C": no decision due to a lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of a very bright phenomenon at low altitude that seemed to follow the witness as he drove: probable observation of the planet Venus and the star Sirius
description: On January 24, 2012, at approximately 7:45 PM, a motorist was driving on a country road when he spotted a very bright, white, cylindrical object that was stationary at a low altitude. The witness stopped his vehicle and signaled. No sound was heard. The motorist continued driving and then noticed that the object seemed to be following him. Returning to his village, he went into his garden and observed that the lights had turned reddish-orange. He then told his wife about his observation and called the police. The police, who arrived at the scene that same evening, found no lights, and the neighborhood inquiry yielded no other witness statements. The observation of a bright point of light low on the horizon that seemed to follow the witness and stopped when he stopped is reminiscent of a celestial body whose direction of observation remained constant (azimuth). In the direction indicated by the witness at the beginning of the observation (around 250° SW) (see the two arrows on the right of the map), the very bright planet Venus (magnitude -3.5) at a low elevation (10°) is indeed visible (see Stellarium map). In the second part of the observation (see the left-hand arrow on the map), the witness observes towards the Southeast: another bright celestial object is clearly visible: the star Sirius, the brightest star in the sky (Mag -1.45), but less bright than Venus, and therefore logically appears more distant to the witness. Given the uncertainty in the observation directions, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of the planet Venus and the star Sirius.

summary: Observations of the atmospheric reentry of a bolide.
description: GEIPAN received numerous reports of a luminous phenomenon in the sky on January 24, 2012, around 7:50 a.m. over the Lorraine region. All of these reports clearly correspond to the observation of a bolide: the entry into the atmosphere of a naturally occurring meteoroid (small asteroid). The Reforme-Meteor network also identifies this event as a naturally occurring bolide. This case is classified as "A".

summary: Observation in the sky of a white trail whose left end turns black: very likely observation of an aircraft condensation trail deformed by wind shear and part of which is not illuminated by the rising sun.
description: On January 20, 2012, at approximately 8:25 a.m., a witness and his daughter observed an unusual aerial phenomenon in the clear sky above the Col de Blaux pass. The witness took photographs of a white plume of smoke, the left end of which turned black before disappearing behind the mountain near the Caire Valley (04). The witness suspected the fall of something that had crashed to the ground but did not see any aircraft or hear any unusual noises. She gave a statement to the police. The police investigation found no traces on the ground, no other witness statements were obtained from residents of the valley, and no signs of controlled burning or fires were found in the area. The hypothesis of a military aircraft could not be confirmed. The gendarmes explained that at this time of year and during this period, the sunrise is low and dazzling, which could explain the change in the smoke's color. This observation has been the subject of several press and online articles. Based on the investigation, three hypotheses were considered: aircraft crash, smoke coming from the ground, and an aircraft contrail (see the investigation report). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": a very probable observation of a persistent aircraft contrail that has been deformed by the wind shear to which it has been subjected since its formation. The gray area is indeed the part that has not yet been illuminated (sunrise).

summary: Observations of orange shapes moving: probable observation of Thai lanterns passing overhead.
description: On January 18, 2012, at approximately 10:45 PM, and again on January 19 at approximately 12:15 AM, a couple observed two sets of orange fireballs silently passing by at a constant speed. The description of orange balls flying silently at a constant speed immediately suggests Thai lanterns. This type of sighting is more common on weekends, but it should be noted that the Chinese New Year on January 23rd may have given rise to numerous celebrations during this period. The weather forecast for Bordeaux indicated a southerly wind, while the witnesses reported a movement towards Bordeaux, suggesting a southwesterly wind. The lanterns could have been launched from one of the many villas or restaurants southwest of La Teste. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of three luminous points forming a dark triangular mass: lack of information.
description: On January 14, 2012, at approximately 9:35 PM, a witness on their fifth-floor balcony was intrigued by three small white points of light outlining a dark, triangular mass. No noise was heard during the very rapid south-to-north movement. The sighting suggested an airplane, with its approach lights illuminated. The primary radar track of aircraft that had flown over the area at that time showed only a high-altitude airliner at 9:48 PM (7 minutes before the estimated time of the sighting, a few kilometers west of the Saint-Quentin vertical axis), but this track was from north to south, while the sighting was in the opposite direction. Therefore, the sighting did not correspond to the aircraft detected by radar. Due to the unique nature of the witness testimony, this case is considered weak; due to the regular and linear movement of the three points of light within the object, this case is considered not particularly unusual. It is classified as "C" due to a lack of information. A more thorough investigation would hardly yield additional information.

summary: Observation of the evolution of a luminous phenomenon in the cloudy sky composed of two cylindrical circles containing luminous round elements: probable observation of a luminous animation produced by a rotating beam sky-tracer.
description: On Monday, January 9, 2012, at 7:02 a.m., a motorist was surprised and intrigued by the movement of two concentric luminous circles in the cloudy sky. These circles were themselves composed of discontinuous, rounded elements. This formation was visible for nearly a kilometer. After two minutes of observation, upon reaching a highway, the motorist could no longer see the phenomenon. No other witness accounts were collected. The near-perfect similarity of the phenomenon described by the witness to the effect produced by certain types of animation projectors strongly suggests this type of origin for the observation (see the investigation notes). The day of the week is unusual for this type of animation, and there was apparently no nightclub nearby, but it could have been a test with rented equipment. However, the phenomenon bears a striking resemblance to the effect produced by this type of projector: see the video Wedding Searchlight Hire Nottingham. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of a light animation produced by a rotating beam sky-tracer.

summary: Observation of a stationary triangular object that appears to be rotating on itself with red and yellow lights: lack of information.
description: On January 2, 2012, a witness observed a triangular object with shimmering red and yellow lights starting at 4:30 PM. The object appeared to rotate at times and then remained stationary. The witness alerted air traffic control in Chavenay, which also confirmed the phenomenon. The observation lasted three hours. No other reports were collected. GEIPAN contacted the Chavenay air traffic control service, and the caller indicated that he had indeed seen a very bright point of light. After a quick analysis, this observation could simply be the planet Venus, and not the object reported by the witness. Also noted that evening was the planet Jupiter near the Moon (see attached astronomical chart). As Venus was quite low on the horizon, its scintillation caused its colors to vary considerably. The witness, contacted again, confirmed that he had indeed identified Venus, that this luminous object was close to the direction of Venus, but remained stationary for two hours, without, however, specifying its precise direction or apparent altitude above the horizon. The observation point corresponds to the Château de Plaisir (Les Saussaies): a luminous tethered balloon could have given the same visual impression. GEIPAN was unable to verify this hypothesis. Given the imprecision of the testimony regarding the observation point, the low unusualness of the case (object stationary for two hours), the absence of photographs despite the length of the observation, and the lack of other eyewitness accounts, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to insufficient information.

summary: Observations of the movement of an object enveloped in a yellow-orange glow.
description: On January 1, 2012, at 1:35 a.m., two witnesses in a car observed the silent, moving motion of an unidentified object in the sky. The witnesses disagreed on its shape but noted a yellow-orange glow surrounding it. The object was then hidden by the forest. The description and its movement, influenced by the wind (see weather report), were consistent with the appearance of a Thai lantern. However, one witness described a triangular shape, while the other described a circular one. Numerous lantern releases occurred that night of January 1, 2012. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent passage in the sky of a red cylindrical shape: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: Recent report (April 12, 2014) of a previous sighting. The witness was waiting for the local fireworks display when he spotted a cylindrical shape with a red light in its center, passing overhead under low clouds. The witness lost sight of the object while going to get his camera. His son took over to follow the object, which disappeared and then reappeared further away. According to the child, the object disappeared, leaving a red trail behind it. Only one report has been collected. The METEOCIEL report for Blagnac indicates very cloudy skies and a strong west wind: 20 to 30 km/h. The object described has characteristics of Thai lanterns (color, duration, speed of movement), but its movement is not consistent with a westerly wind, since it was first observed in the northeast and then in the northwest. However, it should be noted that the observation was not continuous: it could have been two successive, similar objects coming from the west. The hypothesis of a luminous object carried by the wind (Thai lantern) becomes plausible, and even highly probable, given that these lechers are very frequent on New Year's Eve. The appearance described by the witness is unusual for a Thai lantern, which can be explained by the fact that the observations were made through a veil of clouds. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.
